title: Syms Archival Intern
company: Hebrew Union College - Jewish Institute of Religion
description:
About Hebrew Union College

Founded in 1875, Hebrew Union College (HUC) is North America's leading institution of higher Jewish education and the center for professional leadership development of Reform Judaism. With campuses in Cincinnati, Jerusalem, Los Angeles, and New York, HUC educates rabbis, cantors, Jewish educators, nonprofit leaders, and scholars while advancing Jewish scholarship and learning worldwide.

Our mission is to build vibrant Progressive Judaism by educating visionary leaders, advancing Jewish scholarship, and studying Jewish life through an open, egalitarian, inclusive, and pluralistic lens.


Position Summary

The American Jewish Archives (AJA), a division of the Hebrew Union College-Jewish Institute of Religion, seeks a motivated archivist to serve as a part-time Syms Archival Intern. Funded through the generous support of the Sy Syms Foundation, the internship provides hands-on experience in archival processing, digitization, research, and public history programming while helping preserve and promote the history of American Jewish business leaders, entrepreneurs, families, and institutions. The position supports AJA's mission to preserve and make accessible the documentary record of American Jewish life.



Essential Responsibilities:


Archival Processing and Description:

  • Arrange, describe, and rehouse archival collections in accordance with professional archival standards.
  • Create and edit collection inventories and finding aids.
  • Assist with quality control and metadata creation for digitized materials.
  • Conduct preservation assessments and basic conservation activities under staff supervision.


Digitization and Access:

  • Scan archival documents, photographs, and audiovisual materials.
  • Prepare materials for digitization and digital access.
  • Review digital files for completeness, image quality, and metadata accuracy.
  • Assist with uploading and organizing digital collections and related content.


Research Support:

  • Conduct historical and biographical research using archival collections.
  • Assist staff, fellows, and researchers with reference inquiries.
  • Help identify materials related to business history, entrepreneurship, philanthropy, and American Jewish life.
  • Compile research summaries and annotated resource guides.


Programming and Outreach:

  • Assist in developing educational programs, exhibits, lectures, and public-facing initiatives related to The Syms Collection and other AJA holdings.
  • Support events highlighting themes such as first-generation American Jewish entrepreneurs, Jewish family businesses, philanthropy, and the contributions of American Jews to society.
  • Help create promotional materials, social media content, and online exhibits.
  • Assist with tracking program participation and audience engagement.


Scholarly and Digital Projects:

  • Assist with projects that increase awareness and use of AJA's digitized collections.
  • Support initiatives that connect archival materials with contemporary audiences.



Learning Outcomes: By the end of the internship, participants will:

  • Gain practical experience with archival processing and digitization.
  • Develop skills in historical research and archival description.
  • Learn about preservation, access, and digital stewardship.
  • Contribute to public programs and outreach initiatives.
  • Gain exposure to the operations of a nationally recognized archival repository with extensive collections documenting American Jewish history.

title: Senior Sensor Analyst
description:
Responsibilities

Peraton is seeking a Senior Sensor Analyst in our Linthicum, MD office in support of our Department of Defense (DoD) customer as part of a highly talented, highly motivated, and high-performing team. This position offers a unique opportunity to work at the forefront of cyber investigations, digital forensics, cyber threat analysis, and mission support in a dynamic and collaborative environment. The successful candidate will contribute to protecting national security interests by leveraging technical expertise, analytical skills, and innovative problem-solving to address complex cyber challenges. Individuals who are passionate about cybersecurity, committed to excellence, and eager to make a meaningful impact are encouraged to apply.

This Senior Sensor Analyst position conducts intelligence analysis and operational planning to monitor, assess, and report on cyberspace operations. This includes identifying potential threats to Department of War (DoW) critical assets, the DoD Information Network (DoDIN), and Defense Industrial Base (DIB) networks, while supporting the US Intelligence Community and Interagency grid network sensor portfolios. The Senior Sensor Analyst plays a key role in shaping cyber defense strategies, conducting reviews, identifying gaps, recommending solutions, and evaluating large datasets.

As an expert, you will research and evaluate technical and all-source intelligence, focusing on network operations and cyber warfare tactics and procedures related to threats against networked weapons platforms and DoD information networks. Your responsibilities will include analyzing sensor data and network events to assess their operational impact, conducting research on adversary capabilities, and preparing intelligence assessments, technical papers, and cyber threat profiles. Additionally, you will develop and maintain analytical procedures to adapt to changing requirements and ensure effective operations, producing high-quality reports and presentations for senior government officials. If you are a candidate that has Cyber Protection Team (CPT) experience, this position might be a good fit for you.

This position will be fully on site M-F.

Qualifications

  • Minimum of 8 years with BS/BA; Minimum of 6 years with MS/MA; Minimum of 3 years with PhD. A degree in one of these fields is highly desired: Information Technology, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Data Science, Information Systems, or Software Engineering.
  • In lieu of a Bachelors degree, four additional years of relevant experience may be considered.
  • Familiarity with Cloud Security Architecture and all related aspects of cybersecurity operations and analysis (e.g., incident response & management, forensic media analysis, malware analysis/reverse-engineering, and threat intelligence analysis).
  • In-depth knowledge of network and application protocols, cyber vulnerabilities, exploitation techniques, and adversary methodologies (TTPs).
  • Proficient in analyzing various types of network data (e.g., Netflow, PCAP, custom application logs) and employing network sensors to support defensive cyber operations and investigations.
  • Experience with Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) and Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS) for threat detection and response.
  • Familiarity with Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) agents for monitoring end-user devices.
  • Proficiency in Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) forwarders for centralized logging and threat detection.
  • Experience with vulnerability scanners to identify and assess weaknesses in systems and applications.
  • Knowledge of log collectors for managing logs to improve incident response and threat hunting capabilities.
  • Experience drafting and editing finished intelligence, executive summaries, and other papers on key topics and technical scenarios to prepare senior leaders.

Clearance requirement: Active TS/SCI with Poly eligibility.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Professional certifications in good standing: IAM Level II & III, CSSP Analyst (Security +, GSEC, CND, CISSP, CASP+, GCIH, or CEH), or GIAC Certification.
  • Experience with Law Enforcement/Counterintelligence (LE/CI) Operations and/or Cyberspace Operations.
  • Skilled in building extended cybersecurity analytics.
  • Demonstrated experience briefing Senior Executive Service (SES) and General Officer/Flag Officer (GO/FO) leadership.
  • Experience in intelligence-driven defense and/or cyber Kill Chain methodologies.
  • Cyber Network Defense Analyst (CNDA) experience.

title: Quality Assurance Automation, Senior Advisor
description:
Responsibilities

Peraton is seeking a motivated Quality Assurance Automation Engineer to join the BASIS program team. This role is integral to maintaining the program's automation-first QA mandate — all quality assurance activities must be automated. The QA Automation Engineer will develop, execute, and maintain automated test scripts and test cases across the full deployment pipeline, supporting Agile sprint delivery cycles and the Government-managed DevSecOps pipeline. The selected candidate will work provide direction and guidance to engineers and QA leads to contribute to the development of automated test coverage, Requirements Traceability Matrices (RTMs), and UAT support activities, while adhering to rigorous DoD quality standards including zero defects to production, and compliance with DoDI 5000-87.

The position will be responsible for the following but not limited too:

This position is remote

Responsibilities

Test Automation Development & Execution

  • Develop, implement, and maintain automated test scripts for unit, integration, and end-to-end functional testing in accordance with Agile sprint schedules and program quality standards.
  • Ensure all automated test cases are executable by the end of each Agile sprint and delivered for incorporation into the Government-managed DevSecOps pipeline.
  • Support the program's Test-Driven Development (TDD) methodology by writing test cases prior to code development in collaboration with software developers.
  • Analyze the current state of test automation coverage and contribute to the Test Automation State Assessment Report and corresponding automation completion project plan.
  • Automate adjacent legacy test cases per Government-approved schedule to expand overall regression test coverage across the DEERS application portfolio.

Test Planning & Documentation

  • Develop and maintain Requirements Traceability Matrices (RTMs) at the end of each development cycle/sprint, demonstrating complete testing coverage of all requirements.
  • Assist in the preparation of UAT plans, test scenarios, and test scripts for Government and external partner acceptance testing activities.
  • Document all test activities, test case results, and defect findings within the Government-provided Test Case Management System.
  • Contribute to the preparation of Testing Reports, Release Notes, and Software Version Descriptions (SVDs) per release cadence requirements.

Quality Assurance & Defect Management

  • Participate in mandatory code reviews at three checkpoints: 50%, 75%, and 90% of development completion, ensuring conformance to quality standards.
  • Monitor and enforce hard quality thresholds.
  • Triage and track defects in JIRA; conduct analysis, determine if issues were previously identified, and attempt error replication prior to escalation to product teams.
  • Submit JIRA tickets prior to product team escalation; support weekly defect escalation reporting and report escalations to customers and the Government Product Owner at minimum weekly.

Security & Compliance Testing

  • Support application security scanning activities using Fortify, Sonatype, and BURP as part of the pre-production release QA process.
  • Assist in ensuring code scan results are reviewed and documented prior to each production release, when rule packs/STIGs change, and on an as-needed basis.

Section 508 / Accessibility Testing

  • Conduct accessibility testing against WCAG 2.0 Level AA standards at planned intervals throughout the development lifecycle.
  • Assist in the preparation of Voluntary Product Accessibility Templates (VPATs) including test results, remediation reports, and documentation of conformance levels for applicable deliverables.
  • Conduct Section 508 compliance testing and support reporting status to the Monthly Status Report (MSR).

Performance & Environment Testing

  • Support stress and load testing activities conducted in the ProdSim (Production Simulation) environment.
  • Assist in coordinating and supporting Disaster Recovery (DR) testing activities in collaboration with the technical and operations teams.
  • Support Independent Verification & Validation (IV&V) of all application changes in the UAT environment prior to production deployment.

Agile / DevSecOps Participation

  • Actively participate in Agile ceremonies including sprint planning, backlog grooming, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews, and retrospectives.
  • Maintain and update sprint-level defect tracking, test case completion status, and burn-down metrics in JIRA.
  • Adhere to the full deployment pipeline standards and quality gates at each stage.
  • Contribute QA metrics and status to the Monthly Quality Status Report (QSR)

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum of 12 years with BS/BA; Minimum of 10 years with MS/MA; Minimum of 7 years with Ph.D.16 years with HS diploma
  • Obtain and maintain public trust clearance
  • IAM/IAT Level II certification (CompTIA Security+, System Security certified Practitioner (SSCP), CompTIA CySA+ or GIAC Security Essentials (GSEC)
  • Experience in software quality assurance, test automation, or software testing roles.
  • Foundational understanding of test automation principles and experience writing automated test scripts in at least one automation framework or scripting language (e.g., Selenium, JUnit, TestNG, Python, Java, or equivalent).
  • Familiarity with Agile/Scrum development methodologies and DevSecOps principles.
  • Basic experience with defect tracking tools, preferably JIRA.
  • Understanding of software testing lifecycle including unit, integration, regression, and user acceptance testing.
  • Strong attention to detail, analytical thinking, and ability to document test results clearly and accurately.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within a team environment and communicate effectively with developers, leads, and Government stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

  • ISTQB (International Software Testing Qualifications Board) Foundation Level certification or equivalent.
  • Familiarity with Test-Driven Development (TDD) practices.
  • Exposure to static code analysis or dynamic application security testing (DAST) tools such as Fortify, Sonatype, or BURP.
  • Experience with Section 508 / WCAG 2.0 Level AA accessibility testing.
  • Familiarity with ServiceNow for incident tracking and management.
  • Understanding of CI/CD pipelines and automated test integration within a DevSecOps environment.
  • Exposure to Oracle or PL/SQL database environments.
  • Prior experience supporting DoD or Federal government IT programs

Peraton Overview

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees do the can’t be done by solving the most daunting challenges facing our customers. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Target Salary Range

$112,000 - $179,000. This represents the typical salary range for this position. Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual’s experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay.

EEO

EEO: Equal opportunity employer, including disability and protected veterans, or other characteristics protected by law.

title: Senior Export Program Manager
description:
Opportunity

PeopleTec is currently seeking a Senior Export Program Manager to support our Huntsville, AL location.

The candidate will serve as a Senior Export Program Manager within a Project Management Office (PMO) within PAE Fires and will be responsible for providing technical support to the program's Chief Engineer and the Product Manager. The candidate will lead the strategic planning, execution, and stakeholder coordination for Defense Exportability Features (DEF) projects. As assigned defense programs approach critical acquisition milestones (such as Milestone B), the candidate will orchestrate Phase 1A feasibility studies to assess the costs, technology security requirements, and potential benefits of releasing advanced systems to foreign allies while preserving combat overmatch for U.S. forces. The candidate will also identify, scope, and stand up new DEF studies across the broader project office portfolio. The candidate will prepare and present DEF program management findings, reports, and improvement plans to senior management and stakeholders. Will work within and/or lead a multidisciplinary team to achieve program goals. Perform other tasks as assigned by the Chief Engineer and/or Product Manager.

The candidate will be required to interface with internal PMs across PAE Fires and external organizations to include HQDA, ASA(ALT), OUSD(A&S), NIPO, DASA-DEC, SAF/IA, ATEC, AMCOM, and others for coordination and synchronization of DEF program management technical and programmatic objectives.

Duties:

  • Provide technical support and leadership in DEF program management across the system lifecycle (design, development, acquisition, integration, testing, fielding, and sustainment).

The Rigging Helper supports qualified rigging personnel and crane crews with load preparation, gear staging, connection work, load control, placement, and cleanup. Work is performed under direct supervision while the employee develops safe rigging practices, equipment-care habits, signaling awareness, and field hazard recognition. The role stops and reports work whenever the load, rigging, communication, or site conditions do not match the direction given.

Responsibilities

  • Participate in pre-task and pre-lift briefings; confirm the assigned position, task, communication method, and stop signal.
  • Locate and stage slings, shackles, hooks, tag lines, blocking, cribbing, tools, and support equipment in the sequence directed.
  • Check common rigging gear for missing identification and obvious damage; tag or set aside questionable equipment for qualified review.
  • Assist with routing slings, installing hardware, padding edges, preparing pick points, and securing loads under the direction of qualified rigging personnel.
  • Confirm load tags, orientation marks, travel paths, and landing areas are ready; report missing information, blocked access, or unstable support.
  • Maintain exclusion zones, stay clear of suspended loads and pinch points, and use tag lines only from a safe position.
  • Watch for load shift, unexpected tilt, uneven sling tension, snagging, contact, or loss of communication and call stop immediately.
  • Clear travel and landing areas; install or remove blocking only after the load is stable and movement has stopped
  • Assist with de-rigging, post-use inspection, cleaning, coiling, storage, and inventory of rigging gear.
  • Keep rigging bins, trailers, laydown areas, and work zones organized; protect gear from sharp edges, oil, heat, traffic, and ground damage.
  • Support rigging personnel, operators, drivers, and installation crews as directed; report mistakes, damaged gear, missing material, and unsafe conditions promptly.
  • Begin studying rigging and signaling practices in preparation for the certifications required to advance to Rigging 1.

Qualifications

  • Minimum of high school diploma or GED with no prior experience required, or combination of equivalent experience and training.
  • Ability to follow verbal, radio, and standard hand-signal direction and ask for clarification before acting when instructions are unclear.
  • Ability to work outdoors, at heights, around moving equipment, and in physically demanding field conditions.
  • Documented employer practical qualification for assigned rigging duties.
  • Forklift or telehandler, aerial lift or MEWP, and project- or site-specific qualifications when assigned.

title: Senior Level – Production Integration & Implementation Planning
description:
Responsibilities

The Senior Level – Production Integration & Implementation Planning will lead early planning activities required to transition the ClaimsCore solution from Proof of Concept (PoC) evaluation toward a scalable production implementation. You will work across Peraton, CMS, MACs, Cognizant and other technology partners to develop the integrated implementation approach for production, with initial emphasis on Tier 1 interface integration, MAC integration and transition planning, production implementation sequencing, cost modeling, dependency identification, resource requirements, and operational readiness. You will translate lessons learned and technical evidence from the ClaimsCore PoC into an executable production implementation strategy and will be a key contributor to the Production Integrated Master Plan and Schedule (IMPS), Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) analysis, integration planning, MAC transition planning, and other pre-production planning deliverables. The position requires someone capable of operating at both the strategic and execution levels—understanding complex healthcare claims environments while converting technical, operational and stakeholder requirements into a realistic production roadmap.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Lead development of the ClaimsCore production implementation strategy and roadmap, incorporating PoC findings, CMS requirements, technical dependencies, operational constraints, and lessons learned.
  • Lead planning of Tier 1 interfaces: I/F inventory, ownership, dependencies, specifications, connectivity, testing, certification, implementation sequencing and production readiness.
  • Develop the overall MAC integration and transition planning framework, outline the steps to onboard and transition MACs into the future ClaimsCore operating environment.
  • Work with CMS and MAC stakeholders to identify current-state interfaces, dependencies, data exchanges, business processes, transition constraints and readiness requirements.
  • Support development of the Production IMPS, including workstreams, critical path, dependencies, staffing assumptions, stage gates, entry/exit criteria, implementation waves and risks.
  • Develop implementation sequencing recommendations for moving from PoC capabilities through parity, production readiness, MAC onboarding, deployment and stabilization.
  • Coordinate with Data Migration team to incorporate historical data migration, reconciliation, data validation and MAC-specific data transition activities into the production roadmap.
  • Coordinate with Claims Accuracy & Business Rules team on business-rule migration, configuration, regression testing, claims parity and validation activities into production planning.
  • Coordinate with Tech Ops & Security to detail cloud infrastructure, environments, security authorization, performance, disaster recovery, monitoring and operational readiness activities.
  • Coordinate with Change Management to incorporate MAC stakeholder engagement, communications, training, organizational readiness and cutover preparation.
  • Support development of the five-year Total Cost of Ownership model, including implementation costs, infrastructure/cloud costs, licensing, labor, integration, migration, operations/support, MAC transition costs and other major cost drivers.
  • Identify production implementation assumptions and develop low/base/high or alternative implementation scenarios where appropriate.
  • Support development of program staffing and resource models, for stakeholders including Peraton, Cognizant, CMS and the MACs.
  • Facilitate cross-workstream production planning sessions and ensure assumptions, dependencies and decisions are captured and incorporated into the integrated plan.
  • Identify implementation risks early and develop recommended mitigation strategies.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Minimum of 12 years with BS/BA; or 10 years with a MA/MS degree.

  • TriZetto Facets or comparable enterprise claims-adjudication platform experience.
  • Demonstrated experience planning or executing complex production implementations involving multiple systems, interfaces and stakeholder organizations.
  • Strong experience with healthcare payer or government claims-processing environments.
  • Experience with enterprise systems integration, interface planning and implementation.
  • Experience developing integrated implementation plans, roadmaps, schedules and dependency models.
  • Experience coordinating technical, data, operational and business workstreams.
  • Experience developing or contributing to implementation cost estimates, TCO models or business cases.
  • Demonstrated ability to work directly with senior government/customer stakeholders and technology partners.
  • Strong executive communication, facilitation and planning skills.
  • Ability to obtain a Public Trust.

Highly Preferred Qualifications

  • 12+ years of experience managing large-scale healthcare, claims-processing, systems integration, or enterprise modernization programs.
  • Medicare Fee-for-Service or CMS claims-processing experience.
  • MAC operational or systems integration experience.
  • Experience with X12 healthcare transactions, including 837/835 and related healthcare interfaces.
  • Experience with claims-system data migration and business-rule conversion.
  • Knowledge of CMS’ Healthcare Integrated General Ledger Accounting System (HIGLAS)
  • AWS/hybrid-cloud modernization experience.
  • Experience transitioning large government systems from pilot/PoC through production.
  • PMI PMP Certification
  • SAFe/Agile experience in large multi-team programs.

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. title: UNAVAILABLE
description:
Overview

As a patient-focused organization, University of Utah Health exists to enhance the health and well-being of people through patient care, research and education. Success in this mission requires a culture of collaboration, excellence, leadership, and respect. University of Utah Health seeks staff that are committed to the values of compassion, collaboration, innovation, responsibility, integrity, quality and trust that are integral to our mission. EO/AA

This position is responsible for performing routine and preventative maintenance, analyzing mechanical and electrical problems, and performing the appropriate corrective action on equipment in the specified area of expertise. The incumbent is responsible for ensuring the continuous and safe functioning of the equipment in the assigned area. This position is not responsible for providing care to patients.

Corporate Overview: The University of Utah is a Level 1 Trauma Center and is nationally ranked and recognized for our academic research, quality standards and overall patient experience. Our five hospitals and eleven clinics provide excellence in our comprehensive services, medical advancement, and overall patient outcomes.

Responsibilities

Essential Functions

  • Operates, repairs, overhauls, services, and maintains equipment in the area of expertise.
  • Performs regularly scheduled preventive maintenance work on equipment.
  • Helps in designing and implementing mechanical or electrical alterations to new and existing equipment in order to improve efficiency, performance, and to extend the life of the equipment.
  • Ensures that all equipment meets regulatory compliance requirements mandated by local, state, and federal agencies.
  • Maintains clean equipment rooms and other areas.
  • Maintains equipment performance and repair records.
  • May give work direction, establish priorities, and instruct Systems Maintenance Mechanics and other personnel, if lead worker status is assigned.
  • Completes required after-hours on-call rotation.

Knowledge / Skills / Abilities

  • Demonstrated potential ability to perform the essential functions as outlined above.
  • Demonstrated human relations and effective communications skills.
  • Ability to remain calm and think clearly during an emergency situation.
  • Demonstrated computer proficiency.
  • Demonstrated high level of technical expertise.
  • Ability to meet regulatory agency requirements.
  • Ability to determine repair and maintenance methods with limited waste.
  • Ability to devise appropriate solutions to unusual equipment problems.

Qualifications

Required

  • Three (3) years of maintenance and repair experience, or the equivalency in one (1) or more of the following areas: pipefitting, heating, air conditioning, steam-operated systems, pneumatic and electronic building control systems, plumbing and refrigeration systems, commercial or industrial laundry equipment, sterilizing equipment, gas or diesel engines and generators, kitchen and cafeteria equipment, mechanical and electrical troubleshooting, or welding.
  • Completion of two (2) year vocational schooling, if in a refrigeration and air conditioning systems position.
  • Environmental Protection Agency certification with a Universal permit, if in a refrigeration and air conditioning systems position.
  • Depending upon department of hire, a valid, State of Utah Driver's License may be required.

Qualifications (Preferred)

Preferred

  • Boiler license from a regulatory agency may be required for some positions.

Working Conditions and Physical Demands

Employee must be able to meet the following requirements with or without an accommodation.

  • This position involves very physical work that may exert up to 100 pounds and may consistently require lifting, carrying, pushing, pulling, or otherwise moving objects. The position may involve moving heavy equipment and/or supplies. This position involves a variety of physical conditions, such as proximity to moving mechanical parts, electrical current, working on scaffolding and high places, or exposure to chemicals.

Physical Requirements

Carrying, Climbing, Color Determination, Crawling, Lifting, Listening, Manual Dexterity, Pulling and/or Pushing, Reaching, Sitting, Standing, Stooping and Crouching, Walking

title: Director of Regulatory Compliance & Patient Experience
description:
About Us

Specialized Care for the Patients Who Need It Most.

NeuroPsychiatric Hospitals (NPH) is dedicated to providing unparalleled service to our patients, team members, physicians, and families. We dare to do things differently, bringing together compassionate care, specialized expertise, and an interdisciplinary approach to meet the unique needs of those we serve. It is this commitment that distinguishes NPH as the healthcare provider of choice.

As a national leader in behavioral healthcare, NPH specializes in caring for patients with acute psychiatric and complex medical needs. Our hospitals provide patient-centered care through an interdisciplinary, multi-specialty approach, ensuring our patients receive the specialized support they need when they need it most.

With locations in Indiana, Michigan, Texas, Ohio, and Arizona, we are expanding access to our unique model of care across the United States. Join NPH and become part of a team that is daring to do things differently and making a lasting difference in the lives of our patients, families, and communities every day.

Overview

Doctors NeuroPsychiatric Hospital is seeking a Director of Regulatory Compliance & Patient Experience – RN to lead facility-based efforts in regulatory compliance, risk management, patient safety, and patient and family experience. This highly visible leadership role works collaboratively with hospital leadership, physicians, staff, patients, and families to identify and address risks, promote a culture of safety and accountability, and ensure ongoing regulatory readiness. The Director uses clinical expertise and sound judgment to drive meaningful improvements in patient care, safety, and the overall patient experience.

Benefits of joining NPH

  • Competitive pay rates
  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
  • NPH 401(k) plan with up to 4% Company match
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) Programs
  • Generous PTO and Time Off Policy
  • Special tuition offers through Capella University
  • Work/life balance with great professional growth opportunities
  • Employee Discounts through LifeMart

Responsibilities

  • Implement and maintain a comprehensive facility-wide risk management program in collaboration with the Corporate Director of Quality and Compliance.
  • Identify, investigate, analyze, and trend actual and potential risks involving patients, employees, visitors, clinical care, and facility operations.
  • Lead or coordinate investigations of significant incidents, adverse events, near misses, complaints, grievances, and other potential exposures; ensure timely escalation and follow-through.
  • Promote a culture of safety and effective incident reporting; educate staff on risk identification, reporting, mitigation, and prevention.
  • Collaborate with facility leadership and corporate resources to assess potential liability, legal exposure, reportability, and regulatory notification when significant events occur.
  • Develop and maintain systems that support patient safety, proactive risk reduction, and continuous regulatory readiness.
  • Conduct routine and targeted facility rounds, tracers, audits, and mock surveys to identify clinical, environmental, operational, and regulatory vulnerabilities before they become adverse events or findings.
  • Use RN clinical judgment during rounding and event review to identify patient-safety and care-delivery concerns and promptly escalate nursing or medical issues to the appropriate clinical leader.
  • Partner with the Director of Nursing on nursing-related risk and readiness issues without assuming operational authority for nursing services.
  • Review complaints and grievances for patient-safety, regulatory, clinical, legal, and reputational exposure; coordinate timely service recovery and follow-through with patients and families.
  • Maintain a highly visible and accessible presence for patients and families and conduct proactive rounding to identify concerns early and prevent avoidable escalation.
  • Coordinate Root Cause Analyses and other structured reviews for specified events; develop corrective and preventive actions and monitor effectiveness.
  • Lead or coordinate the facility Safety Committee and support QAPI activities using incident, complaint, grievance, survey, environmental, and other risk data.
  • Maintain continuous survey readiness and serve as a key facility resource during state, federal, accreditation, complaint, validation, and follow-up surveys.
  • Coordinate survey requests, documentation, communication, and follow-up activities in partnership with facility and corporate leadership.
  • Assist in development of Plans of Correction and regulatory responses; track corrective actions, evidence of implementation, and sustained compliance through closure.
  • Identify repeat deficiencies, recurring events, high-risk patterns, and ineffective corrective actions and escalate them to facility and corporate leadership.
  • Monitor facility cleanliness, organization, environment of care, safety, and overall presentation; ensure identified issues are assigned, corrected, verified, and sustained.
  • Serve as a resource for risk management, patient experience, performance improvement, policy/procedure development, regulatory readiness, and compliance initiatives; provide regular reporting to facility and corporate leadership.
  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Nursing (BSN) or related healthcare field required. Master's degree in Nursing, Healthcare Administration, Quality, Risk Management, or related field preferred.
  • Minimum two years of experience in healthcare risk management, quality, patient safety, regulatory compliance, or nursing leadership required. Behavioral health or inpatient psychiatric experience strongly preferred.
  • Experience with state, CMS, Joint Commission, DNV, or other applicable surveys required; supervisory experience preferred.
  • Current, active, unrestricted Registered Nurse (RN) license in the state of employment or appropriate multistate privilege required.
  • Strong knowledge of risk management, patient safety, incident investigation, root cause analysis, regulatory and accreditation standards, complaint and grievance management, service recovery, and performance improvement.
  • Ability to identify clinical and operational risks, analyze trends, develop effective corrective actions, and monitor for sustained compliance.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, conflict resolution, organizational, problem-solving, and follow-through skills.
  • Ability to build effective working relationships with patients, families, staff, providers, executive leadership, corporate/legal resources, and regulatory representatives.
  • Comfortable maintaining a highly visible, hands-on presence throughout the facility and addressing concerns proactively and professionally.

title: Irregular Warfare Analyst / Active Top Secret
description:
Responsibilities

Peraton is seeking an Irregular Warfare Analyst for its' Cyber Operations and Analytics programs.

Location: MacDill AFB, FL

Role & Key Responsibilities:

  • The Irregular Warfare Analyst will play a critical role in identifying, analyzing, and disrupting adversarial uncrewed systems (UAS, UUVs, USVs, UGVs) and associated threat networks within the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) Area of Responsibility (AOR).
  • This position requires expertise in counter threat network (CTN) targeting, irregular warfare, and special programs, with a strong focus on interagency collaboration and law enforcement integration to degrade hostile uncrewed system capabilities.
  • You will support a Combatant Command, Directorate of Operations, Interagency Coordination and Targeting Division (ICTD) and interagency (IA) mission partners to coordinate, synchronize, and integrate a wide range of DoD capabilities with IA mission partner authorities directly supporting time-sensitive, dynamic, and deliberate operations and activities that deliver comprehensive, multi-layered actions - sequenced to achieve maximum whole-of-government effects.
  • You will be integrated into a DoD team focused on IW support and collaboration with USG partners.
  • You be the subject matter expert on structured analysis, pattern of life studies, and the fusion of traditional intelligence with unique, structured and unstructured data sources, able to illuminate and exploit enemy vulnerabilities related to proliferation, procurement and weapons of mass destruction networks.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Counter Threat Network Targeting: Identify, analyze, and map adversarial networks that develop, deploy, and support uncrewed systems, including state-sponsored, proxy, and non-state actors.
  • Threat Analysis: Assess the operational employment of uncrewed systems in asymmetric warfare, insurgency, terrorism, and gray zone conflicts across the CENTCOM AOR.
  • Target Development: Prioritize high-value nodes within adversary logistics, procurement, financial, and operational networks for kinetic and non-kinetic targeting options.
  • Intelligence Fusion: Integrate multi-source intelligence (SIGINT, GEOINT, HUMINT, OSINT, MASINT) to build a comprehensive picture of uncrewed system threats and their supporting networks.
  • Special Programs Support: Leverage experience with classified and compartmented programs to enhance operational planning and counter-threat initiatives.
  • Interagency & Law Enforcement Coordination: Work closely with SOF, U.S. government agencies, law enforcement, and international partners to counter the illicit proliferation and operational use of uncrewed systems.
  • Counter-UXS Strategy: Support lethal and non-lethal activities, to include electronic warfare (EW), cyber, and technical countermeasures to neutralize adversarial uncrewed systems and disrupt their supporting networks.
  • Regional Expertise: Maintain deep knowledge of threat actors, procurement pipelines, smuggling routes, and financial enablers linked to uncrewed systems across the CENTCOM AOR.
  • Briefings & Reporting: Produce actionable intelligence assessments, target packages, and strategic reports for senior leaders, operational planners, and policymakers.

* This role is critical in countering uncrewed system threats by targeting the networks that develop, fund, and deploy them, directly supporting U.S. military, allied forces, law enforcement, and interagency operations in the CENTCOM AOR.

Qualifications

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree with a minimum of 8 years of relevant experience.
    • Military service-based training and an additional 4 years will be considered in lieu of the bachelors degree requirement.
  • Extensive experience in counter threat network (CTN) and counter transregional organized crime analysis and targeting, with a focus on uncrewed systems and irregular warfare.
  • Demonstrated experience and background in special programs, compartmented operations, and classified initiatives.
  • Familiarity with CENTCOM operational environment, threat actors, and regional dynamics.
  • Proven ability to coordinate with SOF, interagency partners, and law enforcement to dismantle illicit networks.
  • Proficiency in targeting methodologies, intelligence tools, databases, and analytic tradecraft.
  • Strong ability to synthesize complex intelligence into actionable targeting recommendations.
  • Experience operating in a 4-star military headquarters or an Interagency Partner environment as a staff member with background in the following:
    • Demonstrated experience in developing and supporting DoD strategic and operational Irregular Warfare objectives.
    • Demonstrated experience in working collaboratively with USG Interagency partners.
    • Demonstrated ability to perform all source operational intelligence analysis.
    • Demonstrated ability to deliver unclassified/classified products and parallel reconstructed products tailored to maximize wide-ranging capabilities and authorities.
    • Demonstrated understanding of law enforcement agency organizational structures, functions, data sources, data types, programs, records management requirements.
    • Demonstrated expertise with financial investigative groups that target complex enemy global money laundering, and other criminal financial activities.
  • Good oral and written communications skills, including an expert ability to communicate effectively with intelligence collection requirements at the operational and national intelligence levels.
  • Expert Microsoft Office Skills.
  • U.S. citizenship required.
  • Current U.S. Passport.
  • Active DoD Top Secret security clearance with SCI eligibility.

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Master’s degree and minimum 15 years of experience working in the military All Source Intelligence field.
  • Graduate of a recognized Intelligence Collections Support Course at the Joint or Service Level and Information Operation planning experience.
  • Experience working with distributed teams.

Peraton Overview

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees do the can’t be done by solving the most daunting challenges facing our customers. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Target Salary Range

$112,000 - $179,000. This represents the typical salary range for this position. Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual’s experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay.

description:

Summary

The Spiritual Health Practitioner, Lead provides clinical, operational, and team leadership for Spiritual Health and Pastoral Care services within a person - and family - centred model of care. Reporting to the Director, Spiritual Health and Pastoral Care, the role supports the delivery of compassionate, culturally responsive, and spiritually inclusive care while advancing Providence Health Care’s Mission, Vision, Values, and strategic priorities.

  • Provides leadership and coordination for Spiritual Health and Pastoral Care services, guiding practitioners, on-call resources, and designated staff to support consistent, high-quality person-centred care.
  • Coordinates work activities, contributes to recruitment, conducts performance evaluations, and supports constructive resolution of workplace concerns.
  • Leads program and service development in collaboration with the Director, including planning, implementing, evaluating, and communicating departmental strategic directions, policies, procedures, and initiatives that strengthen the integration of spiritual health across the organization.
  • Delivers comprehensive spiritual and emotional care to patients, residents, clients, families, and staff, including assessment of spiritual care needs, crisis support, and compassionate assistance during serious illness, loss, and end-of-life discussions in ways that respect individual beliefs, cultures, values, and traditions.
  • Advances education, mentorship, and professional development by providing spiritual health education to staff, patients, residents, families, volunteers, and community partners, and by mentoring, supervising, and supporting Clinical Psychospiritual Education interns, residents, students, and other learners.
  • Builds collaborative partnerships internally and within the community, working closely with interdisciplinary health-care teams, community clergy, faith and spiritual leaders, support groups, and other partners to enhance clinical care, education, research, family support, and staff development.
  • Supports organizational responsiveness and continuity of spiritual care by mentoring community faith leaders and volunteers, participating in on-call and back-up on-call responsibilities as required, and responding to organizational emergencies while promoting a safe, respectful, inclusive, and civil environment for all.

What You Bring

Education, Training and Experience

  • Master’s degree in health care, Theology, Public and Pastoral Leadership, Counseling, Spiritual Practices, or a related discipline from an accredited institution.
  • Completion of Clinical Psychospiritual Education (CPE), including an Advanced (Contextual) unit.
  • Certification as a Spiritual Health Practitioner with CASC/ACSS is preferred.
  • One (1) to three (3) years of experience in a leadership capacity.
  • Maintains good standing in a spiritual, religious, or faith community affiliated with the individual’s chosen tradition

Skills and Abilities

  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate with internal and external partners to develop, manage, and evaluate programs, considering client needs, service delivery interrelationships, and service potential within a complex environment.
  • Demonstrated effective leadership abilities.
  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate and negotiate to achieve effective resolution of contentious issues.
  • Demonstrated effective interpersonal skills, including consultation, facilitation, and negotiation.
  • Knowledge of adult learning principles and practices.
  • Demonstrated excellent interpersonal, presentation, and public speaking skills, with keen attention to detail and the ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing.
  • Demonstrated ability to foster effective working relationships that support professional practice and the ongoing development of staff.
  • Ability to build and sustain relationships in a diverse setting.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team and interdisciplinary team.
  • Ability to meet deadlines while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Ability to set priorities and effectively manage competing demands.
  • Demonstrated ability to promote the development of research opportunities and support evidence-based practice within an interdisciplinary, team-based environment.
  • Demonstrated sensitivity to health care settings and organizational culture.
  • Demonstrated ability to provide crisis intervention as required, including responding to Code Blues and other critical incidents.
  • Demonstrated ability to apply counselling theories, interventions, and intentional supportive approaches to support patients, residents, and their families, and to quickly identify the appropriate spiritual health practice to address expressed or unexpressed needs.
  • Demonstrated ability to operate related equipment and technologies, including computer applications, information technology, educational and visual technologies, electronic medical records such as Cerner, pagers, and other communication systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to relate effectively to diverse patient populations and support all expressions of spirituality without imposing personal religious beliefs.
  • Demonstrated ability to approach spiritual health issues in a person-centred manner with insight, discernment, and flexibility.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage stressful situations effectively with sensitivity, compassion, gentleness, caring, and approachability.
  • Ability to work flexible hours.
  • Physical ability to perform the duties of the position.

What We Offer

  • A competitive salary: The salary for this position ranges from CAD $46.37 to $66.66 per hour.
  • Meaningful impact: Your leadership, compassion, and expertise will directly support the spiritual, emotional, and psychosocial well-being of patients, residents, families, and staff.
  • Growth opportunities: We welcome individuals at different stages of their careers and provide opportunities for ongoing professional development, leadership growth, education, mentorship, and learning.
  • State-of-the-art facilities: Work within Providence Health Care’s integrated health-care environment, where spiritual health and pastoral care are valued as important components of person- and family-centred care.
  • Inclusive culture: We respect the dignity, diversity, and interdependence of all people. We value the cultural, spiritual, and religious diversity of our workforce and the patients, residents, families, and communities we serve.

Your Day to Day:

  • Provides leadership to designated Spiritual Health and Pastoral Care staff by setting priorities, managing workload, establishing performance expectations, and evaluating individual and team performance in collaboration with the Director.
  • Designs, implements, monitors, and evaluates Spiritual Health and Pastoral Care programs and services, supporting the department’s strategic goals and Providence Health Care’s mission, vision, values, and commitment to wholistic care.
  • Leads education, professional development, and evidence-based practice initiatives for staff, students, and spiritual health practitioners, while remaining current with CASC/ACSS educational standards and national curriculum developments.
  • Collaborates with internal leaders, interdisciplinary teams, committees, community clergy, spiritual and cultural representatives, and volunteers to strengthen spiritual care services and support organizational priorities.
  • Provides comprehensive spiritual and emotional care to patients, residents, families, and staff, including assessment, counselling, supportive presence, prayer, rituals, memorials, and support during anxiety, loss, death, crisis, and spiritual or existential distress.
  • Supports departmental operations through budget monitoring, policy and procedure development, quality improvement, risk management, health and safety activities, communications, grant applications, reporting, and maintenance of spiritual care activity records.
  • Mentors and supports students, staff, volunteers, and faith-specific visitors, and promotes awareness and respect for diverse spiritual, religious, and cultural beliefs and practices across the organization.
  • Plans and participates in spiritual programs, worship services, memorial services, spirituality groups, educational activities, retreats, awareness events, and other department and facility-wide initiatives.
  • Participates in research and knowledge-development opportunities and promotes the integration of research and evidence-informed practices within Spiritual Health and Pastoral Care.
  • Participates in on-call and back-up on-call coverage and responds to organizational emergencies and crisis situations, including Code Orange and psychosocial disaster response, while providing spiritual health support in accordance with Catholic Healthcare principles and Health Ethics Guidelines

Who We Are: Providence Health Care is one of the largest faith-based health care organizations in Canada. For the people at Providence, living our Mission, Vision and Values means providing British Columbians with compassionate, socially just, exceptional and innovative care every day.

From our humble roots 129 years ago, Providence has grown into globally renowned research, teaching, and care organization. As individuals within a mission-driven organization, we choose to be part of Providence Health Care because we value the organization’s long commitment to social justice and compassionate care, and its commitment to the process of Truth and Reconciliation with Indigenous Peoples.

We acknowledge that Providence Health Care and the new St. Paul’s Hospital site is located on the traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Coast Salish Peoples, including the territories of the xʷməθkwəy̓əm (Musqueam), Skwxwú7mesh (Squamish), and Səl̓ílwətaʔ/Selilwitulh (Tsleil-Waututh) Nations.

description:
Position Summary

Odyssey has an exciting opportunity for a Senior Cost Estimating Analyst to support the Attack Systems Division, Foreign Military Sales (FMS), at Wright Patterson AFB, OH. WID is part of the ISR/SOF Directorate (AFLCMC/WI), who is responsible for equipping our warfighters to win the fight. The Directorate executes a $22 billion acquisition portfolio developing, producing, testing, modifying, fielding, and supporting Air Force ISR and SOF platforms, and related sub-systems. WIDN is AFPEO/WI’s centralized hub for Pre-LOR (Letter of Request) and Case Development for FMS new business efforts. WIDN will provide temporary support to executing Program Management Offices for case execution. Applicants will benefit from competitive salaries, career growth, and a unique ability to positively impact national security on a global scale!

Responsibilities

Duties include, but not limited to:

  • Possess the advanced knowledge, experience, and recognized ability to be considered a highly skilled Cost Estimating Analyst. Must work independently and be able to apply procedures.
  • Utilize cost estimating/analysis techniques, including linear regression, confidence intervals, learning curves, and various estimating methods (analogy, grassroots, actual cost, parametric) to develop cost estimates for all phases of Sensors acquisition programs.
  • Define Work Breakdown Structures (WBS) and Cost Estimating Structures (CES).
  • Perform cost estimating/analysis, including Program Office Estimates (POE), Independent Government Cost Estimates (IGCE), special studies, and milestone reviews.
  • Support the development of life cycle cost estimates, "what-if" estimates, Cost as an Independent Variable (CAIV) analyses, should/will cost reviews, Reduction in Total Ownership Costs (RTOC) analyses, and other economic analyses.
  • Apply knowledge of Acquisition and Financial Management policies, procedures, regulations, and directives, including:
    • Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR)/Defense FAR Supplement (DFARS)
    • DoD Financial Management Regulation (FMR) DoD 7000.14-R
    • Relevant DAFI and DAFMAN guidance on economic analysis, inflation, cost and planning factors, and cost analysis procedures
    • AFLCMC Standard Cost Process
    • MILSTD 881D
  • Utilize automated management information systems and cost-estimating tools, including:
    • Automated Cost Estimating Integrated Tools
    • Parametric Review of Information for Costing and Evaluation "True Planning" parametric modeling
    • Constructive Cost Model
    • Oracle Crystal Ball
  • Ensure data accuracy and maintain the integrity of financial databases.
  • Support program offices in:
    • Program Planning and Budget activities, including developing cost estimates and conducting "should cost"/"will cost" analyses.
    • Analyzing Price and Availability (P&A) data and cost proposals to ensure reasonableness.
    • Identifying and developing program requirements, cost, schedule, technical, and program risks.
  • Prepare program documentation, including program management plans, program baselines, WBSs, and program risk assessments.
  • Adhere to the AFLCMC Standard Process for the Annual Program Office Cost Estimate.

Qualifications

Minimum Required Qualifications

Citizenship: Must be a US citizen

Clearance: SecretEducation/Years of Experience:

  • Master’s or Doctorate Degree in a related field and ten years of experience being performed, five years of which must be in the DoD.
  • OR bachelor’s degree in a related field and 12 years of experience being performed, five of which must be in the DoD.
  • OR, 15 years of directly related experience, eight of which must be in the DoD.

Technical Skills:

  • Expertise in applying regression analysis, confidence intervals, learning curves, parametric models, analogy-based methods, and grassroots estimating techniques to produce defensible cost estimates.
  • Ability to construct, interpret, and apply WBS/CES frameworks in support of Program Office Estimates (POEs), Independent Government Cost Estimates (IGCEs), and milestone reviews.
  • Hands‑on experience with Automated Cost Estimating Integrated Tools, TruePlanning parametric modeling, COCOMO, Oracle Crystal Ball, and other acquisition-related financial databases.
  • Deep understanding of FAR/DFARS, DoD FMR 7000.14‑R, DAFI/DAFMAN guidance, AFLCMC Standard Cost Process, and MIL‑STD‑881D to ensure compliant cost analysis and documentation.
  • Capability to conduct full life‑cycle cost assessments, CAIV analyses, RTOC studies, “should/will cost” analysis, what‑if scenarios, price reasonableness evaluations, and risk‑based cost assessments.

title: Recovery Coordinator
description:
Overview

Change Grow Live are a charity dedicated to the belief that we can make a difference to our Service Users lives, offering support and respect in a safe environment, treating each user as an individual and working with them to find the right treatment and care options.

Our core values are ‘Be open, be compassionate and be bold’ and our team members apply these daily to achieve our mission of helping people change the direction of their lives, grow as individuals, and live life to its full potential.

We are delighted to offer an exciting opportunity for a Recovery Coordinator in Walthamstow. This rewarding and dynamic role is ideal for someone who is passionate about supporting others and ready to make a meaningful impact every day. You will use your skills and experience to assess, engage and empower Service Users, ensuring they access the right support at the right time, in a way that truly meets their needs.

No two days are the same in this role. Each interaction is an opportunity to inspire positive change, making flexibility, curiosity and excellent listening skills essential. If you are motivated by the chance to make a genuine difference and want to be part of a supportive team that values innovation, compassion and courage, this could be the perfect opportunity for you.

Where: Walthamstow

Full Time Hours: 37.5 hours per week

Contract Type: Permanent

Full-time hours at Change Grow Live are 37.5 hours per week. For part-time roles, the salary and payments will be pro rata based on contracted hours.

Responsibilities

About the role:

  • Supporting service users from point of entry into the service and through their treatment/recovery journey
  • Providing screening, assessment, and recovery planning and onward referral
  • Reducing drug and alcohol related harm to service users and the wider community
  • Promoting carer, service user and community involvement
  • Providing advocacy for access to partnership services
  • Working with service users to support social (re)integration, enabling them to lead meaningful and purposeful lives: promoting recovery, resilience, peer support and self-determination
  • Research, design and prepare subject matter and materials for groups / pods.
  • Deliver structured content within group settings to service users at various stages of recovery
  • Engage with debriefing and evaluations with co-facilitators after groups/pods have taken place, reviewing progress and identifying concerns with service users
  • Tailor specific workshops around the needs of the service users.

About you:

  • Have a strong understanding of substance misuse issues and experience of working within a similar field
  • Experience of working with groups/pods and managing group dynamics, such as conflict or challenging behaviour.
  • Be an excellent communicator, both verbal and written with good IT skills
  • Proactive and able to work on own initiative with excellent time management and prioritising skills
  • Have a good working knowledge of mental health interventions, services, and good practice
  • Be a supportive team player with strong interpersonal skills with the ability to work in partnership with a wide range of professionals, agencies, and internal/external stakeholders
  • Ability to manage change successfully in a way that prioritises the needs of service users
  • Understand the importance of information governance processes and commit to follow and apply all necessary safeguards
  • Seek out learning opportunities to improve and broaden your professional knowledge and skills and to contribute and oversee the learning and development of others

What we will give to you:

  • 25 days of annual leave, plus bank holidays. Additionally, you'll receive one extra day of annual leave for each year of service during your first five years, therefore you will enjoy 30 days of leave after five years with us
  • Paid ‘Wellness’ hour each week along with a ‘Wellness’ hub and Employee Assist Programme
  • Contributory pension scheme

title: Data Engineer
description:
Als Data Engineer ben jij verantwoordelijk voor het ontwerpen, bouwen en onderhouden van robuuste data-infrastructuren die de basis vormen voor alle data-analyses binnen de organisatie. Jij zorgt ervoor dat data uit verschillende bronnen op een efficiënte en betrouwbare manier wordt verzameld, opgeslagen en toegankelijk gemaakt voor analisten en data scientists. Je werkt nauw samen met multidisciplinaire teams en speelt een sleutelrol in het realiseren van datagedreven besluitvorming.

In deze functie krijg je de kans om te werken met de nieuwste technologieën en tools op het gebied van big data en cloud computing. Je bent betrokken bij het hele proces, van het definiëren van data-architectuur tot het implementeren van ETL-pipelines en het optimaliseren van database-performance. Daarnaast krijg je volop ruimte om door te groeien naar een senior rol of om je te specialiseren in specifieke domeinen zoals real-time data processing of machine learning engineering. Het bedrijf biedt concrete doorgroeimogelijkheden, zoals het volgen van gecertificeerde trainingen in cloud-technologieën (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) en het deelnemen aan internationale conferenties en kennissessies.

Jouw belangrijkste taken zijn:

  • Ontwerpen en implementeren van schaalbare data-pipelines voor het verwerken van grote hoeveelheden energiedata;
  • Bouwen en onderhouden van data warehouses en data lakes in een cloud-omgeving;
  • Optimaliseren van database-queries en data-modellen voor snellere en efficiëntere analyses;
  • Samenwerken met data scientists en analisten om data-oplossingen te realiseren die aansluiten bij business-behoeften;
  • Monitoren en verbeteren van de kwaliteit, betrouwbaarheid en veiligheid van data-infrastructuren;
  • Implementeren van best practices op het gebied van data governance en data security.

title: Medior Cloud DevOps Engineer
description:
Werken bij het ministerie van Defensie maar niet als militair?

Als je kiest voor een baan bij Defensie, dan kies je voor maatschappelijk relevant werk. Je draagt echt iets bij aan een veilig Nederland. Naast ongeveer 53.000 beroepsmilitairen en reservisten werken er ook nog zo’n 27.000 burgers bij Defensie. Wil jij in je eigen vakgebied als burger bijdragen aan een professionele defensieorganisatie en daarmee aan vrede en veiligheid in binnen- en buitenland?

Als Medior Cloud DevOps Engineer met focus op GitOps zorg jij ervoor dat de Eagle-dienstverlening betrouwbaar, veilig en gecontroleerd van ontwikkeling naar productie gaat.

Eagle levert diverse diensten op het gebied van zoeken, vertalen, spraak en AI. Je kan het zien als een interne conversatie gestuurde zoekmachine (een soort ‘interne Google’). Het helpt medewerkers snel beslissingen te nemen op basis van gekoppelde interne databronnen.

Als Medior Cloud DevOps Engineer met focus op GitOps werk je aan het automatiseren en verbeteren van de manier waarop applicaties en platformdiensten worden ontwikkeld, uitgerold en beheerd. Je helpt teams om sneller, veiliger en consistenter software te leveren door gebruik te maken van moderne DevOps- en GitOps-principes.

Je ontwikkelt en beheert geautomatiseerde deploymentprocessen waarbij Git fungeert als centrale bron voor configuratie, infrastructuur en applicatiebeheer. Je richt CI/CD- en GitOps-processen in, verbetert bestaande workflows en zorgt ervoor dat wijzigingen gecontroleerd, herhaalbaar en veilig naar productie kunnen worden gebracht.

Daarnaast werk je aan de technische basis van het platform. Je automatiseert infrastructuur met Infrastructure-as-Code, beheert het platform, connectoren en draagt bij aan de standaardisatie van ontwikkel- en beheerprocessen. Je werkt bijvoorbeeld met Kubernetes, Helm en tooling zoals ArgoCD of vergelijkbare GitOps-oplossingen.

Je helpt het team om meer zelfstandig te werken door goede standaarden, templates en geautomatiseerde oplossingen beschikbaar te stellen. Wanneer problemen ontstaan, analyseer je de oorzaak en verbeter je processen zodat de betrouwbaarheid en kwaliteit van de dienstverlening verder toenemen.

Je werkt nauw samen met andere DevOps engineers, platformteams, architecten, securityspecialisten en eindgebruikers. Samen bouw je aan een veilige en toekomstbestendige kennis assistent waarin automatisering, samenwerking en continu verbeteren centraal staan.

Je werkt zelfstandig binnen afgesproken kaders, maar staat er nooit alleen voor. Je deelt kennis, denkt mee over verbeteringen en zorgt ervoor dat oplossingen niet alleen vandaag werken, maar ook morgen beheersbaar blijven.

  • Tijdelijke aanstelling met uitzicht op vaste aanstelling
  • Tijdelijke aanstelling met uitzicht op vast.
  • Het genoemde salaris is gebaseerd op een volledige werkweek van 38 uur. Je inschaling wordt gebaseerd op je werkervaring en opleidingsachtergrond.

Dit bieden we nog meer

  • Defensie hecht sterk aan persoonlijke groei en kent goede studiefaciliteiten, hierdoor sta je nooit stil. Je krijgt alle ruimte om jezelf te ontwikkelen en door te groeien.
  • Bij Defensie bouw je elke maand 16,33% van het bruto salaris op in het Individueel Keuzebudget. Je kunt het gebruiken voor het kopen van extra verlofuren of voor fiscale doeleinden.
  • Naast een pensioenregeling bij het ABP ontvang je maandelijks een tegemoetkoming voor woon-werkverkeer of kun je onder gunstige voorwaarden kiezen voor een OV-abonnement met onbeperkt reizen door heel Nederland.

Dit vragen wij

Je bent een praktische DevOps Engineer die energie krijgt van automatiseren, verbeteren en het betrouwbaar naar productie brengen van software. Je hebt ervaring met moderne ontwikkel- en deploymentprocessen en wilt je verder verdiepen in cloud-native technologie en veilige software delivery.

Dit breng je mee:

  • Hbo-werk- en denkniveau: ontwikkeld via opleiding, werkervaring of een combinatie daarvan.
  • GitOps & CI/CD automatisering: Ervaring met Git als centrale bron voor configuratie en deploymentprocessen.
  • Kubernetes & cloud-native technologie: Ervaring met containerplatformen, deployments en beheer van moderne applicatieomgevingen.
  • Infrastructure-as-Code & automatisering: Ervaring met Terraform, Helm of vergelijkbare technologieën.
  • DevSecOps & betrouwbaarheid: Bewust van security, kwaliteitsborging, monitoring en stabiele dienstverlening.
  • Een groeimindset: je vraagt actief om feedback, geeft die concreet en respectvol en zet nieuwe inzichten om in betere code en samenwerking.

Hier kom je te werken

Meer over Commando Materieel en IT

Je komt te werken bij COMMIT (Commando Materieel & IT), onderdeel van het ministerie van Defensie. COMMIT zorgt ervoor dat de krijgsmacht beschikt over het beste materieel en de meest betrouwbare IT-oplossingen. Samen met nationale en internationale partners, waaronder NAVO en EU, werkt COMMIT dagelijks aan de digitale slagkracht van Defensie.

Binnen COMMIT maak je deel uit van de afdeling Besturen & Overige Ondersteuning IT (BOO IT). Deze afdeling levert IT-oplossingen die de bedrijfsvoering van Defensie ondersteunen en zorgt voor de ontwikkeling, implementatie en instandhouding van applicaties en systemen.

Je bent onderdeel van een team van teams dat gezamenlijk werkt aan de Eagle dienstverlening. Denk hierbij aan platform beheer, ranking optimalisatie, product beheer en doorontwikkeling. Het Eagle team is verantwoordelijk voor de dienstverlening op het gebied van Search, Chat en Kunstmatige Intelligentie.

Visie
Het Commando Materieel & IT (COMMIT) ondersteunt de transitie naar een informatie gestuurde en technologisch hoogwaardige krijgsmacht met het beste materieel en de beste IT. Ons COMMITment is groot om de cruciale rol te versterken als strategisch partner van de Commandant der Strijdkrachten, van de operationele onderdelen en van internationale partners. COMMIT vergroot de impact van de ondersteuning door een integrale en innovatieve aanpak van materieel- en IT-projecten, (wapen)systeemmanagement en ketenlogistiek.

Wij investeren in de kwaliteit van onze mensen en de flexibiliteit en diversiteit van het personeelsbestand. De belangrijkste capaciteiten van COMMIT zijn de kennis en ervaring van ons personeel. Om de krijgsmacht sneller te voorzien van materieel en IT zetten wij naast technologische innovatie in op proces- en sociale innovatie op het gebied van projectvoering, inkoop en afstoting van defensiematerieel en personele en logistieke ondersteuning.

Het uitvoeren van innovatieve projecten vraagt om meer samenwerking met het bedrijfsleven, kennisinstituten en andere overheidsorganisaties en maatschappelijke instanties. Onder de vlag van C-COMMIT als National Armaments Director (NAD) ontwikkelen en versterken wij ook de internationale samenwerking op het gebied van materieel en IT (NAVO, EU, multinationaal en bilateraal).

Missie
COMMIT levert de krijgsmacht het beste materieel en de beste IT.

Extra
COMMIT is van iedereen en voor iedereen, we zijn ervan overtuigd dat we met een diverse en inclusieve organisatie onze taak, verbinding maken tussen willen en kunnen, het beste kunnen uitvoeren wanneer ons personeel een afspiegeling is van de maatschappij. Wij nodigen je daarom graag uit om te solliciteren op deze functie!

Defensie zet zich in voor de belangen, welvaart en vrijheid van Nederland. We zijn dagelijks actief in binnen- en buitenland. Onze wereldwijde inzet versterkt de internationale samenwerking en zorgt ervoor dat mensen zich in vrijheid kunnen ontplooien. Nu en in de toekomst.

Bij het ministerie van Defensie werken ongeveer 79 duizend mensen direct en indirect aan vrede en veiligheid. Het ministerie bestaat uit het Commando Materieel & IT (COMMIT), de Bestuursstaf (het departement), de Koninklijke Marine, de Koninklijke Landmacht, de Koninklijke Luchtmacht, de Koninklijke Marechaussee, het Defensie Ondersteuningscommando (DOSCO).

Defensie is een van de grootste werkgevers van Nederland en vertoont overeenkomsten met een groot bedrijf. De operationele commando's (zee-, land- en luchtstrijdkrachten), de Marechaussee, het DOSCO en de COMMIT lijken op werkmaatschappijen.

  • Deze vacature is zowel in- als extern opengesteld. Bij geschiktheid hebben interne kandidaten de voorkeur.
  • Een veiligheidsonderzoek maakt deel uit van de selectieprocedure.
  • Een referentiecheck en assessment kunnen onderdeel uitmaken van de selectieprocedure.
  • Om in aanmerking te komen voor deze functie moet je afkomstig zijn uit een land uit de Europese Economische Ruimte. Mocht dit niet het geval zijn dan beschik je over een gecombineerde vergunning voor verblijf en arbeid (GVVA).
  • Acquisitie wordt niet op prijs gesteld. Wij verzoeken vriendelijk om geen ongevraagde aanbiedingen, telefoontjes of e-mails te sturen. Dank u voor uw begrip.

title: Engineer Intern
description:
About Us

Crux Subsurface, a subsidiary of Quanta Services, Inc. (NYSE: PWR), is a geotechnical drilling company merging innovation with experience to consistently provide accurate data and efficient, constructible solutions to projects of any size.

Our multidisciplinary team combines the expertise of structural and geotechnical engineers with experienced drillers, construction managers, geologists, and quality management specialists.

  • Plans, organizes, and coordinates recreation activities, functional leisure skills, and leisure education
  • Interviews the patient to assess capabilities/interests/barriers. Monitors progress and recommends changes/modifications to program as necessary
  • Designs community reintegration activities to assist the patient with their physical and cognitive needs during physical recreational/leisure activity Assists the patient in understanding their various needs and limitations and how to manage them during function
  • Regularly re-assesses effectiveness of treatment plan, progress of patient towards goals and the need for modifying goals or treatment
  • Communicates patient’s needs and progress to the treatment team, physician, patient, family members, and others as applicable
  • Observes/documents and reports changes in the condition/status of the person receiving services to the Clinical Coordinator, Program Manager or DCM, attending physician and other treatment team members
  • Consults with medical providers regarding patient evaluation & treatment, progress of the patient & discharge from treatment
  • Maintains and submits evaluation, treatment and billing documentation in the format and timelines required by the Company, facility, funding source, local, state and federal regulation
  • Adheres to standards of the Company's Code of Business Conduct, policies, HIPAA and Corporate Compliance programs and appropriate professional practice standards and applicable state/federal laws
  • May work with rehabilitation specialists in fulfilling the patient’s treatment plan through instruction in patient-related activities to be carried out by the rehabilitation specialist with supervision provided by the Therapeutic Recreation Specialist
  • Performs other duties as assigned

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Therapeutic Recreation Therapy, or the equivalent
  • Maintains certification as a Certified Therapeutic Recreation Therapist (CTRT) through the National Council for Therapeutic Recreation Certification (NCTRC)
  • Maintains professional license and/or certification if required by the state in which the CTRS practices
  • Minimum of two years therapeutic therapy experience and therapeutic recreation program design
  • Experience working with patients with neurologic or orthopedic injuries or conditions
  • Demonstrates effective and professional interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills
  • Able to work independently and part of a team
  • Demonstrates strong organization skills and attention to detail
  • Has reliable transportation and can travel to/from multiple assignments/locations on a daily basis

About our Line of Business

Rehab Without Walls, an affiliate of BrightSpring Health Services, is a revolutionary neurorehabilitation program that moves individuals outside the walls of institutional settings and into their natural home and community environment through a continuum of care. It is designed to significantly help people who have primarily experienced a brain injury, spinal cord injury, or stroke/CVA through accident or illness regain functional capabilities. By providing care in the home, community, workplace, or school, Rehab Without Walls promotes greater health through the recovery process, all with industry-leading outcomes that dramatically improve functional skills and independence for patients. For more information, please visit www.rehabwithoutwalls.com. Follow us on Facebook and LinkedIn.

title: Senior Data Engineer (Data Domain Lead) - eMobility
description:
