•Winstdeling van 8% on target (of OTB vast bedrag, afhankelijk van de functie);

•27 betaalde vakantiedagen;

•Flex benefit budget van € 1.800, - per jaar met daar bovenop een extra percentage van jouw salaris. Dit budget kan worden gebruikt voor zaken als aankoop van extra vrije dagen of extra sparen in jouw pensioenregeling;

•Thuiskantoor met laptop, telefoon en een maandelijkse internetvergoeding;

•Hybride werken: thuis of op kantoor, afhankelijk van wat jij nodig hebt;

•Ontwikkelmogelijkheden via trainingen, kennisdelingssessies en inspirerende (netwerk)events;

•Sociale activiteiten met collega’s – van gezellige borrels tot sportieve of inhoudelijke uitjes;

•Een flexibele pensioenregeling, waaraan jij op maat en passend bij jou, bijdragen kan toevoegen.

•Je kunt deelnemen aan de collectieve zorgverzekering.

Lijkt deze job iets voor jou? Ben je klaar om met ons de wereld vorm te geven? Fantastisch! We kijken nu al uit naar jouw sollicitatie.

Sopra Steria is een werkgever die gelijke kansen biedt. Alle gekwalificeerde sollicitanten worden in aanmerking genomen voor een job zonder rekening te houden met leeftijd, afkomst, nationaliteit, huidskleur, verlof voor familie- of medische zorg, geslachtsidentiteit of -uitdrukking, genetische informatie, immigratiestatus, burgerlijke staat, medische toestand, nationale herkomst, fysieke of mentale handicap, politieke voorkeur, beschermde veteranen- of militaire status, ras, etniciteit, religie, geslacht (inclusiviteit), seksuele geaardheid of enig ander kenmerk dat wordt beschermd door toepasselijke lokale wetten, voorschriften en verordeningen. We koesteren een werkomgeving die inclusief is en alle verschillen respecteert.

title: Senior Software Engineer-Decision Logic & Regulatory Workflow
description:
Responsibilities

Peraton's Department of the Interior (DOI), U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS), and NOAA's National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) have identified a critical gap in the federal government's ability to conduct comprehensive Endangered Species Act (ESA) research. While FWS operates an authoritative web-based platform for managing data for terrestrial and freshwater species, it does not currently include NMFS marine and anadromous species data forcing agencies to rely on separate, manual processes. This program closes that gap by integrating marine and anadromous species data into the existing FWS platform, creating a single, unified experience for all ESA-listed species.

Peraton is seeking a Senior Software Engineer to lead the design and implementation of decision logic engine updates and consultation package builder enhancements for a federal environmental platform. You will implement complex regulatory routing logic and species-specific consultation workflows that directly support ESA Section 7 compliance.

This is a fully remote position supporting a 12-month period of performance with potential for follow-on work and possible placement in other programs across Peraton at the conclusion of the program.

Work Location: Remote

Day To Day Roles and Responsibilities

  • Lead the design and implementation of decision logic engine updates for new species types and Endangered Species Act - Section 7 regulatory logic
  • Implement correct species list generation logic for multiple consultation types including marine-only, anadromous, and joint agency consultations
  • Develop agency routing logic to correctly route consultations to the appropriate regulatory agency based on species and project location
  • Incorporate agency-specific content requirements into biological assessment templates within the consultation package builder
  • Validate end-to-end decision logic and template functionality in the non-production environment
  • Support pilot consultation workflow execution, resolving logic defects identified during testing
  • Incorporate live consultation feedback from production into decision logic revisions and consultation package builder updates
  • Contribute to the Consultation Logic Alignment Memorandum, documenting the technical implementation of joint agency consultation logic, species routing rules, and template content requirements for formal government review
  • Deliver Updated DKeys and Consultation Package Builder Assets, incorporating all approved logic changes, template updates, and agency-specific content requirements and submitting finalized assets for government acceptance
  • Submit finalized logic updates to the government for review and acceptance
  • Enforce code review requirements prior to all deployments; maintain all code in the version-controlled repository

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelors degree and 8 years professional experience or a Masters degree and 6 years professional experience or an Associates degree and 10 years professional experience; or a high school diploma/equivalent and 12 years’ professional experience.
  • U.S. Citizenship required; must have the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust clearance
  • Extensive experience with software development with a focus on federal application development
  • Experience developing complex business rules engines, decision logic systems, or regulatory workflow applications
  • Proficiency in Java, Python, or equivalent backend development languages
  • Experience with REST API integration for connecting decision logic engines to cloud data platforms and front-end consultation workflows
  • Experience with federal software development standards including code review, version control, and peer review requirements
  • Experience producing formal technical documentation or compliance memoranda for government review and acceptance
  • Familiarity with federal compliance requirements (Section 508, FedRAMP, FISMA)

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor's/ Master's degree in Computer Science, Systems Engineering, or Enterprise Architecture or a related technical field is strongly preferred
  • TOGAF or equivalent enterprise architecture certification
  • Experience with Databricks, Delta Lake, or cloud data lakehouse architecture on AWS
  • Familiarity with DOI, FWS, NOAA Fisheries, or other natural resource agency IT environments
  • Experience with ESA Section 7 compliance or environmental regulatory systems
  • Active Public Trust Clearance

Peraton Overview

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees do the can’t be done by solving the most daunting challenges facing our customers. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

title: National Tech Trainer
description:
Overview

Position Overview

Location: Vancouver, British Columbia. This role is based in Vancouver and supports the field program nationally, with regular travel across Canadian markets.

Reports to: Senior Director, Retail, Influence Marketing Services, in partnership with the U.S. National Training Manager.

Employment type: Full-time.

The National Tech Trainer leads the design, delivery and continuous improvement of training for Sales Specialists across Canada. The role balances global training content with the realities of Canadian retail — regionalizing programming, spending meaningful time in-store coaching to performance, and keeping training aligned to retailer sales goals.

Training Delivery & Development

  • Design and deliver engaging training programs on client technology (product knowledge, features, benefits, sales techniques, and customer engagement).
  • Conducted in-person and virtual training sessions for part-time brand ambassadors at Retail locations within the assigned region.
  • Develop and maintain comprehensive, up-to-date training materials (presentations, handouts, online resources) that align with the brand's messaging.
  • Adapt training delivery methods to cater to diverse learning styles and ensure effective knowledge transfer.

Coaching & Performance Support

  • Provide ongoing coaching and mentorship to part-time Sales Specialists to enhance their product knowledge, sales skills, and customer service abilities.
  • Observe and evaluate Sales Specialists' performance in-store, providing constructive feedback and guidance for improvement.
  • Identify knowledge gaps and address performance challenges through targeted training interventions.
  • Foster positive partner Field and Store relationships by adapting to local retail store environments, respecting established hierarchies, and adhering to all operational policies while representing Influence Marketing Services.

Program Evaluation & Improvement

  • Assess the effectiveness of training programs through data analysis, feedback surveys, and performance metrics.
  • Monitor sales data and customer feedback to identify areas where training can be optimized to drive sales and improve customer satisfaction.
  • Collaborate with the National Training Manager to align training initiatives with retailers' sales goals and program objectives.
  • Stay abreast of industry trends, new technologies, and competitor activities to ensure training content remains relevant and impactful.

Canadian Market Requirements

  • Based in Vancouver, BC, with the ability and willingness to travel across Canadian regional retail markets, including overnight stays, as program needs require.
  • Dedicated in-store time each month to coach Sales Specialists in the selling environment and drive measurable performance improvement.
  • Regionalize the training approach — adapt global content to Canadian retail environments, retailer expectations and regional market differences.
  • Support bilingual (English/French) program needs in partnership with Quebec-based field leadership.

Performance Measures

  • Training content and materials built on adult-learning principles — clear objectives, effective teaching strategies, evaluation methods and structured plans.
  • Accurate and complete training and onboarding reporting submitted following each session.
  • Consistent monthly in-store field observation and coaching hours completed.
  • Demonstrated improvement in Sales Specialist product knowledge, sell-through and customer experience scores.

Qualifications

  • Technology training background is required — 3+ years designing and delivering product and sales training for consumer technology brands.
  • Experience training within major Canadian retail banners, ideally including Best Buy, Walmart and Staples.
  • Valid passport and the ability to travel to the United States for training, onboarding and program meetings.
  • Proven ability to deliver both in-person and virtual training to distributed, part-time field teams.
  • Strong facilitation, presentation and content-development skills; advanced PowerPoint and Google Slides capability.
  • Comfortable working from data — sales performance, survey results and field observations — to shape training priorities.
  • Valid driver's licence and ability to travel; flexible availability, as travel is at times required on short notice.
  • Strong English communication skills; French an asset.

Job requirements are subject to change at any time at the discretion of the company to align with evolving business needs.

About Influence Marketing

At Influence Marketing, we work for you. As a long-standing partner with clients in the consumer electronics sector, we provide talent who personally connect with our consumers by inspiring participation, creating a memorable brand experience, and influencing future purchasing decisions to form lasting customers.

What You Can Expect From Influence Marketing

We welcome every voice, and we are committed to building a truly inclusive environment where your differences are not just welcomed, they are celebrated. We are always identifying opportunities to encourage our team to be their authentic selves, while working to provide a best-in-class experience for our employees. Whether that is paid holidays, long-term career pathing options, personal development opportunities, or professional stretch assignments, you can expect Influence Marketing to support you.

Influence Marketing's Commitment

We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive organization and are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive equal consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, ancestry, place of origin, ethnic origin, citizenship, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, marital or family status, disability, or any other ground protected under applicable human rights legislation.

Influence Marketing welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities.

Why Join Us?

At Influence Marketing, we believe great work starts with great people. We are committed to building an environment where collaboration thrives, innovation is encouraged, and every employee has the opportunity to grow personally and professionally. When you join our team, you're not just taking a job - you’re becoming part of a culture that values creativity, excellence, and making lasting impressions.

Our Benefits

  • Competitive annual salary
  • Comprehensive health, dental, and vision benefits
  • RRSP program with company contributions
  • Paid time off and statutory holidays
  • Partial mobile phone
  • Leadership Development Program

How to Apply

Please submit your resume and cover letter to: Emily Polson at epolson@influencemarketing.ca

Pay Transparency Statement

We are committed to transparency in our hiring process. The listed salary range reflects what the company is willing to pay for this role, based on skills, experience, and market data.

AI Disclosure

Use of Artificial Intelligence by Recruiters and Hiring Managers

  • At Influence Retail Services Inc. (2025) and Influence Marketing Services Inc., people are at the center of our recruitment process. While we may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools for limited administrative purposes (such as writing creative outreach messages, summarizing interview notes or transcribing reference checks), AI is never the decision maker.
  • Resumes and candidate information are personally reviewed by our recruiters and/or hiring manager, and all hiring decisions are made by people who bring judgment, care, and expertise to each match. If any recruitment process involves a greater degree of AI use during an interview or assessment, we will communicate that to short-listed candidates, so they are aware in advance.
  • Our commitment is to use technology responsibly, while ensuring fairness, transparency, and respect at every stage of the process.

Use of Artificial Intelligence – by Candidates

  • We recognize that candidates may choose to use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support their job search, for example, to refine their writing style or gather research. While this can be appropriate, the information you provide in your resume, screening questions, and interviews must always be truthful and accurately reflect your own experience, knowledge, and competencies.
  • AI should never be used to create or exaggerate credentials. Our goal is to understand the real you – your skills, your story, and your potential – so that we can make the best possible match between you and our company.

title: Program Manager - Senior
description:
Orange Business is here!

About us

Join us at Orange Business!We are a network and digital integrator that understands the entire value chain of the digital world, freeing our customers to focus on the strategic initiatives that shape their business.Every day, you will collaborate with a team dedicated to providing consistent, sustainable global solutions, no matter where our customers operate. With over 30,000 employees across Asia, the Americas, Africa, and Europe, we offer a dynamic environment to develop and perfect your skills in a field filled with exciting challenges and opportunities.

About the role

Lead the successful delivery of NEMO Phase 2 by orchestrating cross-functional teams, managing key program risks and resources, and providing transparent governance and reporting to executive sponsors, ensuring alignment with strategic objectives and business value. • Serve as the single transversal leader accountable for the integrated management of NEMO Phase 2, reporting directly to project sponsors to communicate progress, issues, and decisions clearly and regularly. • Coordinate with Federative Solution Data and Digital technology teams to maintain alignment and coordination across all workstreams, deployment waves, suppliers, and external dependencies. • Define the program charter, scope, governance model, and delivery approach to ensure a controlled transition from Phase 1 and establish clear launch-readiness criteria. • Lead integrated planning and coordination, actively managing milestones, resources, and interdependencies to maintain realistic program timelines. • Implement robust governance, decision-making, escalation, and reporting frameworks; prepare evidence-based materials supporting sponsor and Steering Committee decisions. • Manage program-level readiness, risks, issues, assumptions, and dependencies, including critical topics such as data migration, interfaces, reporting, testing, security, and access controls, ensuring appropriate monitoring and escalation. • Enforce delivery discipline through ownership, validation gates, and sign-off requirements across design, testing, cutover, and deployment activities. • Monitor program budget, resource capacity, and supplier performance, recommending corrective actions as needed. • Ensure the program’s delivery aligns with strategic objectives and delivers expected business value, establishing strong links between workstreams and organizational goals. • Serve as the primary coordination point for executive sponsors, internal stakeholders, suppliers, and critical external partners to facilitate timely information exchange. • Provide consolidated program reporting, support executive decision-making, and escalate major risks or issues promptly to maintain program health.

About you

You bring over 15 years of experience managing large-scale programs, with a strong ability to align technical decisions with business goals. Your expertise includes cloud computing, network observability, data-driven decision-making, and negotiation across multi-disciplinary teams to optimize resources. You recognize the broader impact of decisions, communicate risks clearly to executives, adapt leadership to diverse teams, and maintain focus during project challenges. A master's degree in project management or information systems and relevant certifications like Prosci or Scrum Master strengthen your profile.Your professional skills:• Demonstrate proficiency in managing extensive programs with multiple interconnected workstreams and external dependencies.• Evaluate technical decisions with consideration of their commercial impact to ensure alignment with business objectives.• Exhibit comprehensive understanding of cloud computing, network observability, and software integration patterns to inform program direction.• Apply data analysis techniques to support structured decision-making and effectively communicate insights to executive leadership.• Leverage negotiation capabilities to secure necessary resources and talent across diverse teams, optimizing capacity and performance.Your soft skills:• Recognize cross-project effects of decisions and proactively address potential delays or conflicts to maintain program continuity.• Translate technical risks into clear, actionable business impact statements for communication with C-suite executives.• Adapt leadership approaches to suit culturally diverse teams distributed across multiple geographic locations.• Maintain composure while providing clear structure and direction when facing significant project obstacles.

Join Orange to lead a critical digital transformation program where your expertise in managing complex projects will shape impactful business outcomes. Experience a collaborative environment that values clarity, evidence-based decision-making, and coordinated teamwork across diverse disciplines, supporting your professional growth and contribution to innovative solutions.

What we offer

• Global Opportunities: Work in multi-national teams with opportunity to collaborate with colleagues and customers from all over the world.• Flexible Work Environment: Flexible working hours and possibility to combine work from office and home (hybrid ways of working).• Professional Development: training programs and upskilling/re-skilling opportunities.• Career Growth: Internal growth and mobility opportunities within Orange.• Caring and Daring Culture: Health and well-being programs and benefits, diversity & inclusion initiatives, CSR and employee connect events.• Reward Programs: Employee Referral Program, Change Maker Awards.

Only your skills matter

Regardless of your age, gender identity, race, ethnic origin, religion/belief, sexual orientation, marital status, neurotype, disability, veteran status or appearance, we encourage diversity within our teams because it is a strength for the collective and a vector of innovation. Orange Group is a disabled-friendly company and equal opportunity employer: don't hesitate to tell us about your specific needs.

title: Senior Backend Engineer, Toqi (AI Life Assistant)
description:
Who We Are

You've ordered from Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. That's Prosus, a leading global technology technology company, based in Europe, powering the world's leading lifestyle brands and connecting two billion people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond. We own and invest in 100+ companies across food delivery, quick commerce, fintech and experiences, tied together by an AI-driven ecosystem that delivers seamless, personalised experiences at a scale few companies can match. We've built one of the world's largest agentic workforces. 60,000+ AI agents automating complex workflows and creating the equivalent of 1,000 full-time employees in organisational capacity. Our people don't just use AI. They design it, deploy it, and push what it can do. Through our Ventures business, we're backing the next frontier: AI and commerce, the digital AI workforce, and emerging technologies like robotics, drones and synthetic biology.

Context

Toqi is an AI assistant platform with ~150k users and rapid growth. The system is a monorepo: React
Native (Expo) mobile app, Go API gateway, Python AI agent, Postgres + Redis, deployed on GCP
Cloud Run via Terraform.

The Role

As a Senior Backend Engineer you own services end to end — design, implementation, deployment,
monitoring and the pager. Anything that changes an API contract, a database schema or a cost profile
gets a short design note circulated before the code is written. Judgement calls on data modelling,
failure modes and where to spend the latency budget sit with you rather than being escalated by
default.
Seniority here is measured in what the rest of the team can rely on. You review backend pull requests
with the same care you expect on your own, leave the codebase more legible than you found it, and
raise trade-offs early — where a product request would cost more in reliability, inference spend or
long-term maintenance than it returns, we want that argued rather than absorbed quietly.

Primary Responsibility — API Gateway (Go)

  • Design, build and maintain REST and WebSocket endpoints serving the mobile app and WhatsApp surface
  • Own domain models, repository interfaces, and database migrations
  • Add new handlers and services as product features require
  • Define and version shared API contracts (protobuf) consumed by the client
  • Maintain authentication, authorisation and session handling
  • Enforce rate limits, quotas and abuse protection
  • Instrument services: structured logging, metrics, tracing and useful alerts
  • Keep linters, formatting, and tests passing

Secondary Responsibility — AI Agent Services (Python)

  • Extend the agent runtime: tool calling, orchestration, and third-party or portfolio API integrations
  • Manage prompt and model configuration, versioning, and evaluation harnesses
  • Control inference latency and cost through caching, batching, model routing and token budgets
  • Build and maintain the memory and context layer on Postgres and Redis
  • Handle asynchronous and long-running work: queues, retries, idempotency, dead-letter paths

Tertiary Responsibility — Data, Infra & Cross-Cutting

  • Postgres schema design, indexing, query performance and connection pooling
  • Redis for caching, ephemeral state and pub/sub behind the real-time chat layer
  • Maintain and extend infrastructure as code (Terraform on GCP): Cloud Run services, secrets, IAM
  • Assist with deploys, rollbacks, and environment configuration
  • Implement data retention, deletion and export paths required under GDPR and LGPD
  • Support incident response and write up what happened afterwards

Engineering Practices

  • Branch from dev, open PRs targeting dev, follow Conventional Commits

title: Information Assurance and Security Engineer
description:
Responsibilities

Peraton is seeking a Information Assurance and Security Engineer. The position will be responsible for the following but not limited too:

This position is remote

  • Provide technical and programmatic information assurance services to internal and external customers in support of network and information security systems across the DEERS application portfolio.
  • Design, develop, and implement security requirements within the organization's business processes, including DevSecOps pipelines, cloud migration activities (OCI), and Agile development sprints.
  • Prepare and maintain security documentation using accepted DoD and NIST guidelines, including System Security Plans (SSPs), Security Assessment Reports (SARs), Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), STIG checklists, and implementation plans within eMASS.
  • Prepare Security Test and Evaluation (ST&E) plans and support execution of formal security assessments in coordination with the DMDC Cybersecurity Division (CSD) and Enterprise ISSOs.
  • Provide Certification and Accreditation (C&A) / Assessment and Authorization (A&A) support, including development of security and contingency plans, in alignment with DoDI 8510.01 and NIST SP 800-37 RMF principles.
  • Conduct complex risk and vulnerability assessments; develop and maintain risk mitigation strategies addressing identified weaknesses across the DEERS application environment.
  • Analyze organizational policies and procedures against Federal laws and regulations — including FISMA, NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5, DoDI 8500.01, and OMB M-14-03 — and provide recommendations for closing identified compliance gaps.
  • Recommend and implement system enhancements to improve security deficiencies; support IAVA (Information Assurance Vulnerability Alert) monitoring and monthly resolution activities.
  • Develop, test, and integrate computer and network security tools, including Fortify, Sonatype, and BURP scanning solutions; integrate security scanning into the DevSecOps pipeline for every production release.
  • Secure system configurations and install security tools; scan systems to determine compliance against STIG and NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 baselines; report results and evaluate products and system administration configurations.
  • Conduct security program audits and develop solutions to address identified risks; support 1–3 external audits annually (e.g., DHA MERHCF, DoD CIO ICOFR, FIAR).
  • Provide IA support for the development and implementation of security architectures to meet new and evolving security requirements, including support for OCI cloud migration at DISA IL-4/IL-5 authorization levels.
  • Provide assistance in computer incident investigations; report cyber incidents within 1 hour of discovery per DFARS 252.204-7012 and DMDC IR Team protocols, with follow-up reporting every 24 hours until closure.
  • Perform vulnerability assessments including development of risk mitigation strategies; submit POA&Ms within 3 business days of Category 1 or 2 vulnerability identification and update within 10 business days of vulnerability events.
  • Support Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) activities per NIST SP 800-137/137A, DoDI 8530.01, and DoDI 8531.01, and report weekly vulnerability scan status during Integrated Progress Reviews (IPRs).
  • Maintain and support the program's ATOs and A&I packages through the full RMF lifecycle — Prepare, Categorize, Select, Implement, Assess, Authorize, and Monitor.
  • Implement JFHQ-DODIN and USCYBERCOM Cyberspace Tasking Orders (CTOs) as directed.
  • Ensure all cybersecurity workforce personnel are identified, screened, trained, and certified in accordance with DoD 8140.03 and CMMC (DFARS 252.204-7021) requirements.
  • Conduct and support mandatory security training including OPSEC, CUI Handling, Insider Threat, Privacy Act/PII, IT Security Awareness, Counterintelligence, Antiterrorism Level I, and Records Management.

Qualifications

  • Minimum of 8 years with BS/BA; Minimum of 6 years with MS/MA; Minimum of 3 years with PhD, 12 years with HS diploma
  • Ability to obtain and maintain DOD Public Trust
  • Hands-on experience with the DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) and associated tooling, specifically eMASS (Enterprise Mission Assurance Support Service).
  • In-depth knowledge of NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5, NIST SP 800-37, NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2, NIST SP 800-137, FISMA, DoDI 8510.01, and DoDI 8500.01.
  • Experience conducting vulnerability assessments, developing POA&Ms, and managing the full A&A lifecycle including ATO package development.
  • Experience with application security scanning tools including Fortify, Sonatype, and BURP; familiarity with OWASP secure coding practices.
  • Working knowledge of STIG compliance verification, checklist preparation, and remediation.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting DevSecOps security practices within Agile development environments.
  • DoD 8140.03 / DoD 8570.01-M compliant certification IAT/IAM Level II (e.g., CISSP, CASP+, CEH, Security+, or equivalent certification).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Active Public Trust clearance.
  • CISSP (Certified Information Systems Security Professional) or equivalent advanced certification.
  • Experience with cloud security at FedRAMP Moderate, DISA IL-4, or DISA IL-5 authorization levels; familiarity with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) security configuration.
  • Familiarity with CMMC (Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification) framework and compliance.
  • Experience supporting external DoD financial/operational audits (FIAR, ICOFR, FISCAM).

title: Deputy Program Manager
description:
Responsibilities

Peraton is seeking an experienced Deputy Program Manager (DPM) for the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) Network Operations Center (NOC). The DPB will serve as the second-in-command for a large-scale, mission-critical IT network operations support contract. The DPM organizes, directs, and manages contract operation support functions involving multiple, complex, and inter-related project tasks across geographically dispersed locations. This individual maintains senior-level client relationships, drives program performance, and ensures delivery of all contractual obligations on time and within budget.

The DPM acts with full delegated authority in the absence of the Program Manager and serves as a key liaison between Contractor personnel, government stakeholders, and senior leadership within the CBP organization.

This position requires full-time, on-site presence at the designated CBP NOC facility in Ashburn, VA.

Day to Day Roles and Responsibilities:

  • Program Leadership & Oversight
    • Organize, direct, and manage all contract operation support functions for the CBP NOC program, encompassing multiple complex and interdependent project tasks.
    • Oversee day-to-day operations of contract support teams deployed across multiple sites and operational environments.
    • Assume full Program Manager responsibilities and authority in the PM's absence.

      Lead, mentor, and manage multi-disciplinary teams of contract support personnel at multiple locations, ensuring staffing levels, skill alignment, and performance standards are maintained.

      Organize and delegate responsibilities to subordinates; oversee the successful and timely completion of all assigned tasks and deliverables.

      Foster a high-performance culture aligned with Contractor and government mission priorities.

  • Client Interface & Stakeholder Engagement
    • Maintain and manage the client interface at senior levels of the CBP organization, including SES-level and executive government counterparts.
    • Meet regularly with customer and Contractor personnel to formulate and review task plans, deliverable schedules, and program milestones.
    • Serve as an escalation point for program-related issues, risks, and decisions requiring senior-level resolution.
    • Lead customer discussions with confidence and candor, including difficult conversations about performance, risk, and the path to resolution.
    • Build strong working relationships across Peraton, subcontractor teams, and CBP. Listen to technical staff, remove obstacles, and hold teams accountable without creating friction.
  • Planning & Deliverable Management
    • Collaborate with the Program Manager and functional leads to develop, review, and update Integrated Master Schedules (IMS), Program Management Plans (PMPs), and other contractual deliverables.
    • Ensure all Program Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) elements are properly resourced, tracked, and reported.
  • Schedule, Cost & Performance Management
    • Ensure strict conformance with program task schedules, cost baselines, and performance metrics.
    • Monitor program Earned Value Management (EVM) indicators and other KPIs to identify variances and implement corrective actions proactively.
    • Establish and maintain comprehensive technical and financial reports that communicate program health and progress to both internal management and government customers.
  • Risk & Issue Management
    • Identify, assess, and manage program risks and issues; develop and execute mitigation and contingency plans.
    • Maintain a program risk register and provide regular risk briefings to government and Contractor leadership.
    • Stay close to NOC operations. Understand major incidents, recurring network issues, monitoring gaps, and engineering dependencies well enough to challenge assumptions and guide decisions.
  • Process Improvement & Compliance
    • Ensure all program activities comply with applicable federal regulations, DHS/CBP policies, and contract requirements.
    • Champion continuous process improvement initiatives to enhance operational efficiency, service quality, and cost effectiveness across the NOC program.
    • Identify customer needs and work being performed outside the current contract scope. Bring those findings to the Program Manager and growth team with a clear technical and business case.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications:

  • High School diploma/equivalent and 12 years of experience, including experience in technical leadership, supervision, or management.
  • Must be a U.S. Citizen with the ability to obtain a DHS CBP Clearance.
  • Experience in IT program/project management, with demonstrated experience managing large-scale, complex network operations or IT infrastructure programs for federal government clients.
  • Active Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
  • Demonstrated experience managing teams across multiple locations in a matrixed or distributed environment.
  • Proven track record of maintaining senior-level government client relationships and successfully delivering programs within scope, schedule, and budget.
  • Strong knowledge of IT network operations concepts, NOC environments, ITSM frameworks (e.g., ITIL), and federal IT acquisition/delivery standards.
  • Experience with federal contract management, including FAR/DFAR compliance, deliverable management, and government reporting requirements.

  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical teams through high pressure incidents and build trust with government customers. Must be able to explain complex network issues clearly, work across organizational boundaries, and turn discussions into decisions and follow through.

  • Demonstrated experience with program planning, risk and issue management, resource planning, performance management, and operational oversight.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience supporting DHS, CBP, or other federal law enforcement / border security agency IT programs.
  • ITIL v4 Foundation certification or higher.
  • CCNA or comparable network certification.
  • Experience with Earned Value Management (EVM) and integrated program performance reporting.
  • Active DHS Suitability or CBP-level background investigation.
  • Direct experience with enterprise network engineering, NOC operations, or network architecture is strongly preferred.

Peraton Overview

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees do the can’t be done by solving the most daunting challenges facing our customers. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual’s experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay.

title: Data Engineer DSV
description:
3 redenen waarom dit jouw baan is

  • Krijg energie van data met impact en draag bij aan een datagedreven SVB
  • Ontwerp en bouw end-to-end datapipelines die onze organisatie elke dag slimmer maken
  • Versterk het Service Center Data (SCD) op ons hoofdkantoor in Amstelveen

3 redenen waarom dit jouw baan is

  • Krijg energie van data met impact en draag bij aan een datagedreven SVB
  • Ontwerp en bouw end-to-end datapipelines die onze organisatie elke dag slimmer maken
  • Versterk het Service Center Data (SCD) op ons hoofdkantoor in Amstelveen

Jij doet het

Je helpt onze Directie Sociale Verzekeringen (DSV) om de juiste inzichten te verkrijgen zodat zij betere beslissingen kunnen nemen. Als Data Engineer bij het Service Center Data (SCD) ben je verantwoordelijk voor het ontwikkelen en testen van verschillende dataverladingen. Data engineers leveren een bijdrage aan de zogeheten geborgde straat. Dat wil zeggen; de data wordt verladen en getransformeerd ten behoeve van dashboarding, gestandaardiseerde analyses en self service BI. Samen met collega’s in verschillende rollen werk je aan de ontwikkeling en optimalisatie van informatieproducten (bijvoorbeeld analytics, rapportages en dashboards). Je stuurt op herbruikbaarheid, privacy, datakwaliteit en tijdigheid en draagt actief bij aan de ambitie van de SVB om datagedreven te werken. Je werkt op een kort cyclische manier (Agile Scrum) nauw samen met ontwikkelaars en product owners om de backlog scherp te krijgen. Je bent inhoudelijk betrokken bij functionele en acceptatietests, voert checks uit en denkt mee over wat getest moet worden. De testcoördinator is verder verantwoordelijk voor de planning en uitvoering.

Concreet zijn de taken van de Data Engineer de volgende:

  • Ontsluiten van data uit verschillende type bronnen (API, CSV, database)
  • Toepassen van transformaties op de data met behulp van SQL en Python
  • Ontwikkelen van Synapse pipelines voor het verladen van de data
  • Testen en valideren van dataverlading
  • Monitoren en troubleshooting
  • Technisch onderhouden van Synapse pipelines
  • Samenwerken met Report engineers, Cloud Engineers, Data modelleurs en Informatieanalisten om datamodellen te valideren en de data-infrastructuur te optimaliseren
  • Technisch uitrollen van datamodellen in brons, zilver en goud.

Jij bent het

Je bent iemand die onafhankelijk en zelfstandig kan werken, maar verliest daarbij de samenwerking nooit uit het oog. Je werkt graag met focus en gestructureerd. Je schakelt moeiteloos tussen business en je collega’s en weet belanghebbenden mee te nemen in je denkrichting.

Als Data Engineer heb je de volgende algemene kennis en vaardigheden:

  • Kennis van de basis architectuur principes en stijlen van Data Warehousing en Business Intelligence (Inmon, Kimball).
  • Kennis van en tenminste 5 jaar ervaring met het toepassen van SQL voor gestructureerde (tabellen, kolommen en relaties) data.
  • Kennis van en meerjarige ervaring met het toepassen van PySpark voor gestructureerde (tabellen, kolommen en relaties) data.
  • Kennis van CI/CD en versiebeheer in DevOps.
  • Duidelijk en helder kunnen communiceren over de mogelijkheden en beperkingen aan stakeholders.
  • Ervaring met ODI is een nice to have.
  • Leergierig en open om nieuwe technologieën te leren en te implementeren.
  • Goede teamgeest, je neemt collega data engineers mee in de gemaakte producten en brainstormt over innovatie op het gebied van data engineering.

Daarnaast beschik je over:

  • HBO werk- en denkniveau
  • Minimaal 5 jaar ervaring als Data Engineer in een complexe data omgeving
  • Uitstekende beheersing van de Nederlandse taal in woord en geschrift
  • Ervaring met MS Azure

Welke kansen bieden we jou?

Jouw uitdaging, balans en groei: het heeft onze aandacht. Kansen en mogelijkheden om te groeien als persoon en als professional zijn er genoeg. Aan jou de taak om ze te pakken. Ook kan jij bij start als Data Engineer (op basis van een 36-urige werkweek) rekenen op:

  • elke maand maximaal € 6.395,00,- brutosalaris (fulltime is bij de SVB 36 uur per week).
  • 16,33% individueel keuzebudget. Jij kiest zelf hoe je dit inzet: wil je bijvoorbeeld meer salaris, een sabbatical, meer pensioen opbouwen of meer verlofdagen? Aan jou de keuze.
  • ruim 5 weken vakantie.

Er is nog meer. Ga voor een compleet overzicht naarwww.werkenbijdesvb.nl/vacatures/arbeidsvoorwaarden (http://www.werkenbijdesvb.nl/vacatures/arbeidsvoorwaarden)

Jouw werkomgeving

Van kinderbijslag tot AOW-pensioen: namens de overheid en samen met 4.500 collega’s maken we het mogelijk om de volksverzekeringen uit te betalen. Dat betekent dat we elk jaar 62 miljard euro overmaken aan zo’n 5,7 miljoen mensen. Op tijd, eerlijk en efficiënt.

Je werkt binnen het Service Center Data van de directie Bedrijfsvoering. Hier werk je in een domeinteam en vakgroep waar inhoud, samenwerking en kwaliteit centraal staan.

Samen bouwen jullie aan herbruikbare en toekomstbestendige dataoplossingen. Je denkt mee over standaarden, leert van collega’s en draagt actief bij aan de ambitie van de SVB om meer datagedreven te werken.

Jouw werk doet ertoe. De inzichten die jij helpt realiseren ondersteunen besluiten die impact hebben op miljoenen mensen in Nederland.

Bij de SVB werken we bewust. We kijken samen vanaf welke plek jij het beste resultaat behaalt. Is dat op kantoor in Amstelveen, vanuit huis of op een andere plek? Dat stem je af met je team en leidinggevende.

De SVB wil een diverse en inclusieve organisatie zijn, waar iedereen zich thuis voelt. Een afspiegeling van de samenleving. Onze doelgroep is immers ook divers. Teams met diversiteit waar iedereen ertoe doet maken ons effectiever, creatiever en zorgen voor betere dienstverlening.

title: Technical Project Manager
description:
Riverside Overview

Riverside Research is an independent National Security Nonprofit dedicated to research and development in the national interest. We provide high-end technical services, research and development, and prototype solutions to some of the country’s most challenging technical problems. All Riverside Research opportunities require U.S. Citizenship.

Position Overview

Riverside Research is seeking a Technical Project Manager to advise, assist and support the United States Space Force at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, OH. This individual will support process development and documentation in the development and deployment of National Space Intelligence Center (NSIC) space and counter-space models and data management supporting policy makers, the operations community, and the acquisitions community.

Responsibilities

  • Provide project management and integration support to align mission priorities, technical activities, and enabling functions critical to the National Space Intelligence Center (NSIC) and related enterprise-level functions.
  • Support and execute stakeholder engagement, mission planning, task management, schedule integration, documentation control, information management, and workflow execution across areas such as requirements development, test and evaluation planning, funding and contracting execution and policy and governance development in areas such as threat modeling, simulation, and analysis (MS&A), data and infrastructure planning, and future capability evaluation and integration planning.
  • Apply structured project management practices, enterprise integration methods, acquisition lifecycle awareness, and practical process improvement skills to ensure activities remain visible, aligned, traceable, and executable in support of mission objectives.
  • Provide advice, assistance, and support to the NSIC on the development and integration of digital engineering and modeling, simulation, and analysis processes to support organizational activities
  • Assess current processes, data, and supporting capabilities to identify new, integrated capabilities for the digitization of the NSIC mission
  • Advise on the potential benefits and uses of advanced tools and bring awareness to related efforts across USSF functions while fostering collaboration and streamlining integration of NSIC developed data and models
  • Work closely with NSIC leadership, project officers, technical teams, and mission stakeholders to track actions, manage integrated schedules, coordinate decision packages, maintain shared knowledge repositories, and advance program priorities.
  • In collaboration with a team, develop and coordinate processes, governance and training documentation in line with Department of War, Intelligence Community and industry standards.
  • Develop collaborative relationships with NSIC internal and external stakeholders
  • As part of a team, maintain flexibility to perform other duties as assigned

Qualifications

Required

  • Top Secret clearance with SCI adjudication
  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, or equivalent experience
  • 5+ years of experience in technical project execution and management
  • Knowledge of methods, techniques, and processes supporting the digitization, integration, and optimization of processes, system components, infrastructure requirements, user experience design features, and test and evaluation methods.
  • Proven analytical and creative problem-solving abilities
  • Experience composing documentation, reports, and briefings for program baselines, decision makers, and status for senior leaders
  • Ability to manage time independently without direct supervision

Desired

  • 2+ years of Department of War MS&A experience
  • Experience and knowledge of the DoW’s planning, programming, budgeting, and execution (PPBE) cycle with specific experience drafting budget request and justification proposals
  • Knowledge of complex information technology analysis concepts, functions, techniques, and capabilities to evaluate the feasibility of proposed new systems, applications, and tools and ensure successful integration with existing and anticipated infrastructure and digital environments.
  • Knowledge of data science principles, techniques, and tools, including data-driven algorithms, statistical methods, data analytics, data modeling and simulation, data visualization, IT systems, and emerging technologies (artificial intelligence and machine learning).
  • Experience with one or more of the following:
    • Simulation environments: AFSIM, NGTS, ITASE, JSE, or relevant tools
    • Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) modeling and tools
    • Computer Aided Design (CAD) modeling and tools
    • C++, Java, MATLAB, SIMULINK, SysML or similar programming language

Global Comp

100,000 - 150,000 This represents the typical compensation range for this position based on experience, location and other factors.

Closing Statement

Riverside Research Institute is a not-for-profit, technology-oriented defense company, where service to our customers and support of our staff is our overall mission. Riverside is an affirmative action-equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws regarding recruitment and hiring. Riverside offers comprehensive compensation and benefit packages to our employees. Riverside bases its employment decisions solely on technical experience, qualifications and other job-related criteria related to our organizational purpose as a not-for-profit company, and without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex marital status, sexual orientation, national origin, physical or mental disability, veteran’s status or any other status legally protected by applicable federal, state, and local law.

title: Recovery Worker
description:
Overview

At Change Grow Live, our commitment to making a difference in the lives of those who use our services is unwavering. We provide support, respect, and a safe environment, where we tailor our approach to each individual's needs to find the best treatment and support options.

Our core values are ‘Be open, be compassionate and be bold’ and our team members apply these daily to achieve our objective of helping people change the direction of their lives, grow as individuals, and live life to its full potential.

We have an exciting opportunity for a Recovery Worker who has the skills and experience to assess and engage with our service users, ensuring that they access the right intervention at the right time, in a way that best meets their needs.

With this role you’ll be working as part of the recovery team, based in Gravesend. The team supports people with their or their loved ones’ drug and alcohol issues.

Where: Gravesend

Hours: 22.5 per week

Contract Type: Permanent

Full-time hours at Change Grow Live are 37.5 hours per week. For part-time roles, the salary and payments will be pro rata based on contracted hours.

Responsibilities

About the role:

  • Supporting service users from point of entry into the service and through their treatment/recovery journey
  • Providing screening, assessment, and recovery planning and onward referral
  • Reducing drug and alcohol related harm to service users and the wider community
  • Promoting carer, service user and community involvement
  • Providing advocacy for access to partnership services
  • Working with service users to support social (re)integration, enabling them to lead meaningful and purposeful lives: promoting recovery, resilience, peer support and self-determination
  • Research, design and prepare subject matter and materials for groups / pods.
  • Deliver structured content within group settings to service users at various stages of recovery
  • Engage with debriefing and evaluations with co-facilitators after groups/pods have taken place, reviewing progress and identifying concerns with service users
  • Tailor specific workshops around the needs of the service users, such as: anger management, sleep disorders, relationships, etc

About you:

  • Have a strong understanding of substance misuse issues and experience of working within a similar field
  • Experience of working with groups/pods and managing group dynamics, such as conflict or challenging behaviour.
  • Be an excellent communicator, both verbal and written with good IT skills
  • Proactive and able to work on own initiative with excellent time management and prioritising skills
  • Have a good working knowledge of mental health interventions, services, and good practice
  • Be a supportive team player with strong interpersonal skills with the ability to work in partnership with a wide range of professionals, agencies, and internal/external stakeholders
  • Ability to manage change successfully in a way that prioritises the needs of service users
  • Understand the importance of information governance processes and commit to follow and apply all necessary safeguards
  • Seek out learning opportunities to improve and broaden your professional knowledge and skills and to contribute and oversee the learning and development of others

What we will give to you:

  • 25 days of annual leave, plus bank holidays. Additionally, you'll receive one extra day of annual leave for each year of service during your first five years, therefore you will enjoy 30 days of leave after five years with us.
  • Paid ‘Wellness’ hour each week along with a ‘Wellness’ hub and Employee Assist Programme
  • Contributory pension scheme
  • Several benefits incl. discounts for shopping, cinema, holidays, etc.
  • A friendly and supportive team
  • Training, career development & progression opportunities
  • Generous Refer-a-Friend Scheme

Please ensure that when completing your application form and supporting statement, you reflect on the details outlined in the job description. This will help us understand how your skills and experiences align with the requirements of the role.

AI can be a really helpful tool when putting together your application, and we're happy for you to use it. However, what we're most interested in is you.

We want to understand your experiences, achievements and strengths, so please make sure your application reflects your own story and clearly shows how you meet the essential criteria and the impact you've made in previous roles.

There's no need to write in a particular style. The strongest applications are those that are authentic, specific and clearly demonstrate your skills, experience and potential. We look forward to learning more about you.

Direct applications only — we will not be engaging agencies for this vacancy.

Please note: This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK at the time of application. For applicants with time-limited visas, unfortunately, we are unable to support new visa applications or extensions.

title: Services Electronics Technician
description:
About Kinematics:

Kinematics creates motion control solutions for mission-critical systems in demanding environments. Based in the U.S. with six global manufacturing centers and seven service centers, we reliably deliver on diverse customer needs and have the manufacturing expertise to deliver any volume cost effectively.

For close to three decades, we have been innovating solutions and working closely with our customers to provide the most reliable, bankable drives across multiple industries. Today, with over 3 million drives and 1 million electronic controllers globally deployed, representing hundreds of millions of hours of operation, we are proud of our role in sustainably supporting critical applications across the industrial, satellite and solar sectors.

Kinematics was founded in 1996, has over 750 employees globally, is headquartered in Phoenix, AZ, with sales offices in North America and Europe, and manufacturing operations in the United States, China, Mexico, and Spain.

Job Title: Services Electronics Technician

Reporting to: Service Center Manager

Position Location: Phoenix, AZ

Job Description

Position Summary

The Services Electronics Technician diagnoses, repairs, tests, and validates electronic products used in renewable energy and industrial motion-control applications. This role supports service-center operations through component-level troubleshooting, accurate service documentation, spare-parts control, customer technical support, and occasional field service. The ideal candidate combines strong hands-on electronics capability with a disciplined commitment to safety, quality, responsiveness, and customer satisfaction.

Key Responsibilities

· Receive, identify, and process incoming electronic devices using barcode, serial-number, and customer asset-tracking information.

· Perform diagnostic testing, fault isolation, and root-cause analysis on printed circuit board assemblies, controllers, embedded systems, and related electronic products.

· Troubleshoot and repair equipment at board and component level, including surface-mount (SMT/SMD) and through-hole components.

· Read and apply electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, bills of materials, assembly drawings, and product service instructions.

· Use electronic test equipment, including digital multimeters, oscilloscopes, bench power supplies, and applicable communication or network diagnostic tools.

· Complete functional testing and validation to verify that repaired products meet defined safety, quality, and performance requirements.

· Document failure analysis, repairs, parts usage, test results, and disposition decisions in service and quality systems.

· Prepare repair recommendations, technical findings, and service quotation inputs for customer review.

· Support service-level commitments for safety, quality, turnaround time, responsiveness, and on-time return of repaired units.

· Prepare repaired products and associated documentation for shipment back to customers.

· Maintain accurate inventory of spare parts, replacement units, repair materials, and consumables; initiate replenishment requests when needed.

· Provide troubleshooting support to customers, field personnel, and technicians at other service centers.

· Participate in customer and internal meetings concerning RMA status, repair planning, recurring failures, and corrective actions.

· Collaborate with Engineering, Quality, Operations, and Supply Chain to address product issues and improve service processes and product reliability.

· Travel periodically to customer sites and solar photovoltaic installations to diagnose, repair, upgrade, commission, or rework equipment.

· Follow all company, customer, ESD, environmental, and site-safety requirements.

Required

Licenses Required

Preferred

Working Conditions and Physical Demands

Employee must be able to meet the following requirements with or without an accommodation.

This position involves standing for extended periods of time and is not exposed to adverse environmental conditions.

Listening, Manual Dexterity, Pulling and/or Pushing, Sitting, Speaking, Standing, Walking

title: Mechanical Test and Fluid Systems Engineer
description:
TDI Technologies, Inc. is seeking an early- to mid-career Mechanical Test & Fluid Systems Engineer to provide hands-on engineering support to the Navy Surface Warfare Center Philadelphia Division (NSWCPD) Machinery Technology and R&D organization. The engineer will support research, development, testing, and evaluation of submarine hull, mechanical, and electrical (HM&E) systems and components, with particular emphasis on fluid systems, flow testing, acoustics, machinery testing, and experimental engineering.


The successful candidate will provide engineering support to the Machinery Silencing RDT&E Branch Fluid Labs Group and associated test facilities, including the Quiet Flow Test Facility and Shipboard Hydraulic Laboratory.


Responsibilities will include test planning and design, development of test procedures, test execution, instrumentation and data acquisition, fluid-flow and acoustic measurements, engineering analysis, troubleshooting, and preparation of technical reports.


This position is well suited for an engineer who enjoys applying mechanical engineering fundamentals to real-world experimental problems and is comfortable working directly with test equipment, fluid systems, instrumentation, machinery, and engineering personnel. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to the design and execution of testing, interpret experimental results, identify and troubleshoot problems, and provide engineering recommendations.


Benefits

Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Disability Insurance, Voluntary Benefits, 401K, Tuition Assistance, Paid Vacation, Paid Holiday, and Paid Sick Leave.


Key Responsibilities


Test Planning, Design, and Execution

• Develop and support detailed test plans for operational, hydraulic, fluid-flow, acoustic, and machinery testing of submarine HM&E components and systems.

• Provide engineering input to the design and configuration of laboratory and test-site setups.

• Develop and document test procedures, operating instructions, and safety procedures necessary to conduct testing safely and effectively.

• Review test objectives, equipment requirements, instrumentation requirements, expected operating conditions, and

anticipated test results prior to test execution.

• Support test readiness reviews and other technical reviews associated with laboratory and test-site operations.

• Execute approved test procedures and provide hands-on engineering support during test operations.

• Monitor test activities and equipment operation to identify unexpected conditions, anomalies, or performance issues requiring engineering attention.

• Document test activities, observations, equipment conditions, operating parameters, and test results.

• Support test planning and scheduling activities and coordinate with government engineering, laboratory, and technical personnel.


Fluid Systems and Flow Testing

• Apply mechanical engineering and fluid mechanics principles to the analysis and testing of hydraulic and fluid-flow systems and components.

• Support testing and evaluation of submarine HM&E components, including valves, flow-control components, CORDs, and related systems.

• Evaluate fluid-flow performance, pressure, flow rate, differential pressure, and other relevant operating parameters.

• Assist with the design, modification, installation, operation, and troubleshooting of fluid test systems and associated laboratory equipment.

• Identify potential sources of abnormal system behavior, flow instability, vibration, noise, or other performance issues.

• Provide engineering recommendations related to test configuration, equipment operation, component performance, and troubleshooting.

• Work collaboratively with Fluid Labs subject matter experts and engineering personnel to resolve technical issues encountered during testing.


Acoustic Testing and Analysis

• Support the acquisition, processing, and engineering evaluation of acoustic measurements obtained during operational and flow testing.

• Evaluate acoustic test results against established operational thresholds, requirements, or expected performance.

• Support the setup, verification, and operation of acoustic sensors, instrumentation, and associated data acquisition systems.

• Analyze acoustic and vibration-related test data to identify trends, anomalies, and potential sources of excessive noise or vibration.

• Apply fundamental principles of acoustics, vibration, fluid mechanics, and mechanical systems to interpret experimental results.

• Support engineering investigations into machinery, fluid-flow, and component-generated acoustic phenomena.

• Communicate acoustic test results and engineering findings to government and contractor engineering personnel.


Instrumentation and Data Acquisition

• Configure, operate, troubleshoot, and maintain laboratory instrumentation, sensors, and data acquisition systems used during mechanical, fluid, and acoustic testing.

• Verify instrumentation and data acquisition equipment are properly configured and functioning prior to testing.

• Select and apply appropriate measurement techniques and instrumentation for engineering test requirements.

• Assist with troubleshooting sensors, transducers, DAQ hardware, signal-conditioning equipment, and associated test instrumentation.

• Maintain appropriate documentation of instrumentation configuration, calibration status, test setup, and measurement requirements.

• Utilize C324 data acquisition systems to configure and record test data during test execution.

• Review collected data for completeness, consistency, validity, and indications of anomalous test conditions.


Engineering Analysis and Technical Evaluation

• Perform engineering analysis of experimental test results using appropriate mechanical engineering, fluid mechanics, and acoustic principles.

• Evaluate test data to determine component and system performance relative to test objectives and expected operating conditions.

• Identify trends, relationships, anomalies, and significant findings within experimental data.

• Compare test results against established requirements, baseline performance, theoretical expectations, or previous test results when appropriate.

• Develop engineering calculations, plots, tables, and other technical analyses to support evaluation of test results.

• Use MATLAB, Excel, or other engineering analysis tools as appropriate to support data processing and engineering evaluation.

• Apply engineering judgment to determine whether test results are technically reasonable and whether additional testing or troubleshooting may be required.

• Communicate engineering findings and recommendations to project engineers, government technical personnel, and other stakeholders.


Engineering Design and Troubleshooting

• Provide engineering support for the design, modification, installation, operation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of HM&E laboratory and test systems.

• Assist in developing practical engineering solutions to test-system, equipment, instrumentation, and component problems.

• Review engineering drawings, schematics, equipment specifications, test configurations, and technical documentation.

• Identify potential improvements to test setups, instrumentation, procedures, and equipment.

• Support repair and modification activities associated with laboratory and test equipment.

• Work with engineers, technicians, and laboratory personnel to implement and verify engineering solutions.

• Provide engineering recommendations based on test results, observed equipment behavior, and applicable engineering principles.


Technical Documentation and Reporting

• Prepare technical documentation describing test objectives, test configuration, procedures, instrumentation, operating conditions, results, analysis, and conclusions.

• Prepare and review post-test technical reports and engineering deliverables.

• Develop charts, plots, tables, calculations, and other engineering presentations of test results.

• Maintain clear and traceable documentation of test activities, engineering analyses, equipment configuration, and technical decisions.

• Prepare supporting documentation for Mission Readiness Panels and other technical reviews as required.

• Participate in technical meetings, design reviews, test readiness reviews, and post-test reviews.

• Present technical findings and recommendations to engineering personnel and other stakeholders as required.


Laboratory and Engineering Support

• Support preparation, setup, operation, modification, and teardown of laboratory test equipment and machinery.

• Maintain laboratory equipment and test setups in a safe and operational condition.

• Support troubleshooting and resolution of test equipment, instrumentation, machinery, fluid-system, and facility issues.

• Follow established laboratory, engineering, quality, security, and safety procedures.

• Work collaboratively with mechanical, electrical, acoustics, fluid systems, test, laboratory, and other engineering personnel.

• Perform additional engineering analysis, testing, design, and laboratory support activities as assigned.


Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or an equivalent engineering discipline from an ABET-accredited college or university.

• Minimum of three (3) years of relevant engineering experience.

• Professional experience with mechanical testing, fluid systems, fluid flow, acoustics, vibration, or related experimental engineering activities.

• Demonstrated understanding of fundamental mechanical engineering principles, including fluid mechanics and mechanical systems.

• Experience developing, reviewing, or executing engineering test plans and procedures.

• Experience with laboratory or field instrumentation, sensors, transducers, and/or data acquisition systems.

• Ability to interpret engineering drawings, schematics, test procedures, technical documentation, and equipment specifications.

• Ability to analyze experimental data and apply engineering judgment to evaluate test results.

• Experience troubleshooting mechanical systems, test equipment, instrumentation, or fluid systems.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with engineers, technicians, laboratory personnel, government personnel, and project management.

• Ability and willingness to perform hands-on engineering activities in a laboratory and test environment.


Clearance & Certifications /Special Requirements

• U.S. citizenship required; must possess or be able to obtain a Secret clearance within 90 days of hire.

• Must have a valid US passport or the ability to obtain one upon position acceptance.

• Due to the nature of our work with the U.S. Department of Defense, U.S. citizenship is required. Some positions may require the renunciation of any non-U.S. citizenship to obtain and maintain a security clearance.


Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with fluid-flow testing, hydraulic systems, or experimental fluid mechanics.

• Experience with acoustic testing, noise measurement, vibration testing, or machinery silencing.

• Experience evaluating acoustic data against operational or engineering requirements.

• Experience with valves, flow-control devices, piping systems, hydraulic components, or other HM&E equipment.

• Experience developing test-site configurations or providing engineering design guidance for laboratory testing.

• Experience troubleshooting mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, or fluid flow systems.

• Experience with laboratory data acquisition systems and instrumentation.

• Experience with pressure, flow, temperature, vibration, acoustic, or other engineering measurement systems.

• Experience with MATLAB, LabVIEW, Python, Excel, or other engineering analysis and test-support software.

• Experience supporting naval, maritime, submarine, defense, or other government engineering programs.

• Experience with submarine hull, mechanical, and electrical (HM&E) systems.

• Familiarity with engineering test and evaluation processes.

• Familiarity with technical reviews, test readiness reviews, and post-test reporting.

• Familiarity with Navy laboratory, test facility, or shipboard engineering environments.


Work Environment

This is a full-time, on-site engineering position located at the Philadelphia Navy Yard. The position requires a combination of hands-on laboratory and test activities and office-based engineering analysis and documentation.


The engineer should be comfortable working directly with machinery, fluid systems, piping and components, instrumentation, sensors, acoustic measurement equipment, and data acquisition systems. The position may require participation in test setup, equipment installation or modification, troubleshooting, test execution, and teardown activities.


Because the position supports work requiring access to classified information, an active Secret security clearance is required. Candidates with strong mechanical engineering fundamentals and relevant experience in fluid mechanics, acoustics, mechanical testing, experimental engineering, or HM&E systems are encouraged to apply. Experience supporting Navy or defense programs and experience working in laboratory or test environments are highly desirable.


Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is an early- to mid-career mechanical engineer who enjoys applying engineering fundamentals to hands-on testing, troubleshooting, and design problems.


The candidate should have a strong foundation in fluid mechanics and mechanical systems, with practical experience or demonstrated interest in acoustics, vibration, fluid-flow testing, or experimental engineering. This individual should be comfortable moving between the laboratory and engineering office—helping design a test setup, configuring instrumentation, operating and troubleshooting equipment, executing testing, evaluating acoustic and fluid-flow results, and documenting engineering conclusions.


The successful candidate will be a technically curious, hands-on engineer who can work independently, communicate effectively with government and contractor personnel, and use engineering judgment to turn experimental observations and test data into useful engineering conclusions and recommendations.


Equal Employment Opportunity Policy

TDI Technologies, Inc. provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.
